chapters.title: Chapter 673: Kent vs Kaizo (1)
paragraphs: "Master, do you want to exchange a few punches with me?" Kaizo asked with a grin. The fact that he had become powerful was a key reason why he wanted to meet Kent in a punch-out.
This was his way of showing his master that he had become stronger and that he was now ready to go on missions. Of course, he had always wanted to be on missions.
Kent looked at Kaizo for a few minutes and then scanned him...
⟦Name: Kaizo⟧
⟦Bloodline: True Divine Angel (25%)⟧
⟦Realm: Core Formation (Peak)⟧
⟦True Realm: Spirit King⟧
⟦Body Cultivation: Diamond⟧
⟦Rank: SSS+⟧
⟦Job Class: Divine Thunderborn Berserker⟧

’So his true realm after the upgrade was actually at the spirit King stage, but has been suppressed. I guess using high-quality bodies to upgrade him wasn’t so bad. This will give him a head start when I ascend to a higher world.’
Kent smiled and then stood up. "But of course, Kaizo, you will be a good sport."
Kaizo grinned and then moved, appearing on one of the many training grounds in the legion tower. Kent also moved and stood opposite him.
The distance between them was not that wide, showing that the clash would be instantaneous. Of course, it would be a spectacle, considering they wouldn’t be using their weapons, only their fists.
...Well, Kaizo’s fist was his weapon... But Kent wouldn’t be using his sword or dagger, considering he had fallen in love with daggers after recalling Faceless Memories.
He stood and locked gazes with the grinning Kaizo, who already had golden lightning dancing across his body.
Around the training ground, the legion moved to watch what was about to happen. Nathan, now known as Krex, was among them.
Over the past years, he had spent every single second trying to come to terms with his role as Kent’s servant. He struggled to come to terms with that.
At the end of every pondering, he only arrives at a singular answer, which is to engage in a battle with Kent, who would have to prove himself worthy to be called his master.
So now, he wanted to see what Kent was capable of against Kaizo, the third strongest among them. Kent had yet to add him to a legion simply because he didn’t know which one of them to add him to.
The undead are basically undead beings, so it wasn’t like he could join them. As for the Night Riders, he also didn’t qualify to join them.

The Eternal Wrath has its unique origins, which are from the last floor of every dungeon. The Soul Sentinels also have their lineage, so he could only stand on the sidelines and, perhaps soon enough, his legion name would be made known.
But for now, he just wanted to see Kent’s prowess.
"Who do you think will win?" Ankaara, the ice elemental, asked.
"Of course, Kaizo will win. He has basically become a menace since his upgrade, and now that he has gained a true name, I can’t wait to see how he trash Master—"
Gorzak, who was the first to fall after Kaizo’s upgrade, said with a booming smile. The others smiled, watching this. The Barbarian King just seemed too attached to Kaizo after his defeat.
"I say Master has this in the bag," Aetheris said, looking at Kent’s small figure standing against Kaizo’s bigger frame.
"I think Master will win too," Skoggr said, looking curiously at Kent. In fact, this was their first time seeing Kent about to clash with someone after he single-handedly killed seven Spirit Kings...
Aside Aetheris, the rest didn’t see him do that...so they are actually looking forward to this fight...
"Are you ready?" Kent asked.
"Born ready," Kaizo responded... "Created ready, I mean."

With that, they both moved, and their fists met in a resounding clash. Lightning burst, filling the place. Kaizo uses lightning, and so does his master, Kent, so it was a thunderous boom that shook the training ground.
Kaizo’s golden lightning is powerful. However, Kent’s doesn’t pale in comparison..
Strangely, after he went through Chaos’ memories, his lightning was slowly changing from golden to red.

Kaizo struck yet again, his fist blazing with thunder as he launched a lightning-infused jab. Kent barely dodged the strike, which whipped past his cheek and tore a small crater into the training ground. The ground trembled beneath their feet.
"That was close," Kent smiled, watching the ground crack open wide. The force behind the punch was enough to snuff a Sovereign off their mortal coil.
But Kent just smiled...
Kent countered immediately, closing the gap with a flurry of punches. Each blow was precise, his fists moving with a speed that blurred them into streaks of motion.
Kaizo blocked and parried, his own fists radiating thunderous energy that cracked the air. He was an expert in hand-to-hand combat after all...so this was his field.

However, Kent was once known as Chaos, one of the strongest brutes to have ever lived. He was also proficient in hand-to-hand combat using his fist. Countering Kaizo’s punch was merely child’s play for him.
The clash of fists sent shockwaves rippling through the legion tower. Every strike resonated like a hammer on steel. Dust and small stones exploded outward from where their fists collided.
However, whenever the ground was obliterated, it promptly healed itself. Also, while the punches could accidentally kill them, the tower was a place you couldn’t just die, even if you wanted to.
So the two were not fearing for their lives as they threw punches at each other.
Kaizo’s lightning fists surged with power, glowing brighter with every strike. He unleashed a series of brutal hammer fists, each blow meant to break Kent’s arms.
But Kent’s body moved with perfect balance, absorbing the impacts, his own fists striking back with blistering speed and unyielding force.
Kent’s right hook landed squarely on Kaizo’s jaw, sending a ripple through his body. Yet Kaizo barely staggered, his grin widening as golden lightning flared wildly over his skin.
Kaizo spun low and launched a sweeping blow, his fist cutting through the air like a bolt of thunder. Kent ducked, the strike smashing into the training ground, shattering the stone beneath him.
It rebuilt the next second.

With a roar, Kent exploded upward, delivering a devastating uppercut charged with his shifting lightning aura—the blow connected with Kaizo’s chest, sending him flying backward with a thunderous crash.
Kaizo slammed into a pillar but pushed himself up instantly, lightning crackling violently around him. His eyes burned with fierce determination.
"Not bad," Kaizo said, licking a trickle of blood from his lips. "But I’m just getting started."
Kent smiled calmly, muscles tensing for the next exchange. Around them, the legion held their breath, witnessing the battle of two lightning warriors whose fists could tear mountains.
One was muscular, and the other looked like he was competing for the next Miss Universe.
The pure fist fight had only just begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 674: Kent vs Kaizo (2)
paragraphs: "Eat my fist...master." Kaizo jumped high into the air and descended with a thunderous boom. Kent crossed his hands on his chest and took the blow, sending him staggering back.
But Kaizo was upon Kent the next second.
His fist was coated in lightning, just like Kent’s, but Kaizo’s was much more potent, and every time he punched him, the force behind his punch kept sending Kent staggering backward.
Kent, of course, was handling the punch like a champ, making it seem like he wasn’t bearing the force behind Kaizo’s punch when, in fact, he was feeling something.
The punches contain both pain and terrifying force. Whenever Kaizo’s punch lands on Kent’s body, he feels some excitement in his bones.

This suggests that something else was at play, leaving him wanting more. After a while, he knew what was making him giddy. It turns out that getting punched isn’t too bad when you’re a body cultivator.
⟦Your body is growing stronger from the energy absorbed⟧
Every few minutes, Kent receives this message, and after each message, he becomes stronger. This caused him to be on the receiving end of Kaizo’s fist.
⟦Your body is growing stronger from the energy absorbed⟧
"Kaizo, at this point, if you dont get serious, I will fall asleep from being tickled by you," Kent said with a grin, when the next message appeared.
"Oh, I am just getting started," Kaizo’s voice boomed as his fist crackled with more energy. His hair even stood on end, showing he is using more lightning energy this time.
There was no skill to the fight; it was pure brute strength. However, when Kent saw the fist coming, he knew it was a dangerous one. However, he didn’t dodge.
Instead, he also changed his energy and punched out.
Boom
Crack

Kent heard the cracking sound come from his right arm, indicating his arm had broken, more like the bones in his right hand had shattered. His hand went numb, and then, like he expected, blood started seeping from his fist.
Kaizo broke his arm, but the smile on Kent’s face doesn’t mimic someone whose arm is broken. In fact, the smile conveys a hint of gratitude.
Naturally, Kent was indeed grateful to Kaizo for helping him break through to the Diamond Body cultivation.
⟦Congratulations, you are now a Diamond Body Cultivator⟧

This means his physical strength has skyrocketed, indicating that he has achieved his goal. He felt like he was close when he started absorbing Kaizo’s punches...so seeing the message now, he became happy.
Kent looked at his broken arm, and a smile appeared on his face. "That was dangerous, Kaizo, but now it is my turn to fight back."

Kent activated his Chaos Dragon bloodline, covering his arm with dragon scales. The broken arm straightened and healed in a couple of seconds. This demonstrates the remarkable power of Kent’s bloodline.
"Here I come," Kent’s speed exploded, and before Kaizo knew it, he was in front of him. He punched forward, landing a powerful punch on Kaizo’s chest.
He was too late to react, as Kent’s speed far surpassed his own. However, even though Kent’s speed hadn’t exceeded his own, he would still have struggled to defend against the punch.
It contains more power than in his human form.
This threw Kaizo flying back. But Kent didn’t allow him to land. He moved swiftly across the floor, appearing behind Kaizo.
He punched up, meeting Kaizo’s back. The punch sent him flying forward again. This time, Kent allowed Kaizo to land on the ground.
Kent studied his fist for a second and then looked at Kaizo, who was radiating a golden energy.
His presence grew stronger, and while he hadn’t activated any skill, the strength emanating from him was enough for Kent to know he was about to unleash his bloodline.
"You might want to start using your bloodline now, master. The next punch contains 5% of my bloodline," Kaizo warned before he moved.
His punch crackled with energy.
It became much denser, and judging by the runes around his arm, he was indeed using his bloodline, just a portion of it at least...

But that was enough to create a sonic boom around his fist when he punched out. Kent, who saw this, knew he had to protect himself, so his body was immediately coated in dragon scales, most specifically, his chest.
Then he also punched out.
However, before their fist could even meet, the shockwave being produced was enough to send someone like Krex flying back.
"How is this even possible?" Krex wondered, sitting far from the training ground. The shockwave coming from the two punches is more than he can bear.
Even someone like Gorzak was exerting all of his strength so that he could stand still.
"Observe, brat...this is how real men fight," Gorzak responded with a thunderous laughter, one that blended with the sonic boom being created from the two punches.
The world seemed to have slowed down somehow as the two fists came close to meeting each other.
Even the other legion watching the battle felt their bodies getting pushed back, long before Kent and Kaizo’s fists met.
When they did, a sonic boom, one that carried enough energy to obliterate the training ground and send the legion flying back, resounded.
BOOM!
Kent and Kaizo were thrown backwards, bearing the pressure from each other’s punches. Kaizo, in particular, was sent flying far from Kent.
Kaizo’s arm is broken, bent at an unnatural angle. Golden blood was coming from a couple of cracks on both his arm and chest, and even his face had a few crack marks.
Most parts of his fist lost the flesh, and, looking closely, one of his bones, which looked golden instead of white, has some cracks on it...
That bone has been tempered using Kaizo’s True Divine Angel bloodline, so that one is much stronger than the rest.
However, it still has cracks in it. This shows just how powerful Kent’s punch was.
Kent, on the other hand, was staring at his fist with a dazed look on his face. There was not even a single wound on it. It was like his fist punched nothing.
His body looked perfectly fine, and aside from the force from Kaizo’s punch that entered his body, he looked fine.
’This can’t be possible, right...this shouldn’t be possible, right?’ Kent wondered, raising his head to look at the wrecked Kaizo, who stood up wearing a smile on his face.
Despite his body being injured, he doesn’t seem concerned about his injuries...
"Master, how much of your bloodline did you use..." Kaizo instead wants to measure his strength against his master. He lost, but he wants to know..
Kent scratched the back of his head with his left hand as a guilty expression appeared on his face. "Uhhhm...I used 1%..."
Kaizo fell back on his ass...shocked written all over his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 675: Ankaara’s Curiosity [Bonus]
paragraphs: "No way..." Gorzak appeared in the healing training ground, took Kent’s scaly fist, and started examining it.
"No way that was just 1%," Gorzak said, not believing it one bit. He is a body cultivator whose body has already reached the stage of Sage Body cultivation.
And thanks to recalling some of his memories, he knew how to utilize their bloodline strength in combat.
Also, now that his bloodline had awakened and even strengthened, he wanted to ask Kaizo to spar with him; to see who had the strongest body and bloodline.
He had high hopes that his bloodline would be able to counter Kaizo’s overwhelming strength despite being just a Diamond Body cultivator.
He knew Kaizo was stronger; in fact, as someone from a race that respects brute strength, he held Kaizo in high esteem.
But hearing that Kent used just one percent of his bloodline to obliterate Kaizo’s 5% bloodline—that just didn’t seem realistic or sound authentic to Gorzak.
And he wasn’t the only one. All the legion just couldn’t believe that one percent of their master’s bloodline was strong enough to counter and even overpower Kaizo’s 5% bloodline.
They surrounded him like tigers.
However, what they dont know is that Kent was more shocked than they were.
"I am not lying because, while it may sound so unbelievable, I can only channel 1% of my bloodline... my body is still too weak to handle more than 1%," Kent smiled, saying that.
He may have awakened 16% of his bloodline, but despite being at the Diamond Body cultivation stage, he can only channel 1%.
Kaizo had already started healing quite fast, so he moved closer and examined Kent’s fist like his brothers and sisters were doing.
After a few minutes, he smiled. "That was dangerous, master... I expected you to also use 5% of your bloodline to counter mine... but to think that just 1% is already this monstrous..."
Kaizo shook his head and smiled.
"Master, may I ask, what is your bloodline?" Nykali, the Shade King, asked.
The only reason they would truly believe was if their master showed evidence. Using just one percent of his bloodline was too incomprehensible to them.
"Nothing flashy about my bloodline... but since you asked, then why not?" Kent smiled. "I have the Primordial Chaos Dragon Bloodline... in other words, I am a Chaos Dragon."
They nodded...
"Dragons are naturally powerful, so it is no wonder the master was able to wreck Kaizo," Zharkaz, the dragon general, said, smiling at Kaizo.
The brute just ignored him.
Of course, the others were the same. Although they had no idea what it meant to be the Chaos Dragon, they knew that dragons, like Zharkaz, have stronger bloodlines and bodies.
Although Zharkaz was a dragon too, he was all talk and no show.
Kaizo gave him a good beating during their fight. Perhaps, now that he had awakened his bloodline, he would have some luck when they faced each other again.
But for now, they all seem to come to terms with the fact that Kent indeed used just 1% of his bloodline.
Of course, they didn’t have their memories, so knowing about the Chaos Dragon was impossible. If only they knew they were in the presence of royalty.
Well, there was one person among them who had her memories intact...
Ankaara eyed Kent for a few seconds, thinking.
’He can’t be him, right... I mean, from what my mother told me... the Chaos Dragon was the strongest being to have ever lived... Master Kent is just... not there.’
She narrowed her gaze at Kent, but regardless of how much she thought, she couldn’t come to terms with Kent being the Chaos Dragon.
’Mother said the Chaos Dragon vanished and hasn’t been seen again. She never said he died... so this can’t be him... maybe his descendant.’
’But what if he is him... what if he truly is the Chaos Dragon who reincarnated?’ This question left her wondering many things. It felt both conflicting and oddly intriguing to find out.

’Asking him won’t hurt... but how should I ask him without making it seem like I’m being nosy... though on the other hand, if he is the Chaos Dragon, that will explain using 1% of his bloodline to shatter Kaizo’s arm and wreck his body.’
After thinking for a while, Ankaara decided to ask...
"Master, I have a question... You can choose not to answer if it is too personal." Kent nodded. "Go ahead, Ankaara."
"Are you in any way related to the infamous Chaos Dragon that stood at the peak of power during the Primordial Era?"
After giving it careful thought, she devised this approach. It encompassed everything. This wouldn’t make her appear nosy, but even if it did, the question seemed general enough.
Kent could choose not to answer, and it wouldn’t look like he had disappointed her... but she truly needed an answer.
This was because, while she believed in Kent and knew one day he would help her get her revenge on her family, having the Chaos Dragon as her master would boost her confidence even further.
Kent studied her expression for a few seconds and then smiled. "Before I answer your question, tell me what you know about the Chaos Dragon."
Instead of answering, he asked for more context. Ankaara was eager to answer Kent’s question before he even asked it.

"I know that he existed during the Primordial Era. Some say he came from a world called Lumen, while others claim he originated from the Primal Abyss. However, one common thing is that people are aware of him and that he was terrifyingly strong.

I don’t have much authority to open the ancient scrolls, but from what I know, his legend has gone on for millions of years. Some even called him the Father of Body Tempering, while others claim he paved the way for body cultivators to attain godhood.
However, as I said, I’m not familiar with him. I just have bits and pieces of his legend... but he was a dignified person nonetheless."
Kent smiled and then smirked. Slowly, he burst into resounding laughter. His legion watches him with puzzled looks.
"First off, that bastard was no dignified person. I mean, what kind of brute goes about slaughtering left, right, and center without even asking a question?

His mind is all about fighting and slaughter. So, calling him dignified is the last thing you should," Kent smirked. "Though I have to say, he was indeed a good body cultivator... a terrific one at that, and he was indeed powerful.
But, jeez, to think he would be classified among dignified legends. I mean, what were these people thinking, spreading false rumors about me..." Ankaara’s eyes widened.
"Nice meeting you, Ice Fairy. I go by many names... You can call me Kent, which is my real name, by the way. But I was also known as Chaos back in the day..."

chapters.title: Chapter 676: Unexpected [Bonus]
paragraphs: Ankaara’s jaws were hanging when Kent introduced himself as the Chaos Dragon... He didn’t want to say anything at first, but knowing Ankaara knew something about his first Incarnation made him compromise.
Who would have thought he would learn he was a dignified person?
...That sounded funny considering the memories Kent had of himself as the Chaos Dragon, which doesn’t portray him as a dignified person. If anything, he should be called a blood demon instead.
All that bastard did was talk about who he had killed and who he would be killing next. Such a lifestyle shouldn’t be dignified at all.
But that was just Kent’s opinion of himself, after recalling just a small piece of his memory — it was even one of the reasons why he wanted to answer Ankaara’s questions.

Unlike Valtor, who only had rumors after the Faceless Assassin, Ankaara actually knew something, so he sought outside opinions on how people perceived him. It turned out he was an existence more unusual than he expected.
"No need to look shocked... I was once the Chaos Dragon... But I am Kent now, so relax a bit," Kent smiled, looking at the Ice Elemental lady’s shocked expression.

"The Chaos Dragon, huh... I know of a Chaos Dragon... I learned that he was the most fearless person who had ever lived. Some even say he was the only person to ever walk through a doom gate and enter the unknown universe, kill to his heart’s content, and come back... unscathed."
Skoggr paused, then a frown appeared on his face. "How did I know that?" he asked, looking at Kent and his friends.
Naturally, Kent also wore a look of puzzlement. What had just happened? "Did you just get a piece of your memory back?" Kent asked, and Skoggr moved through his memories, only for his eyes to widen.
"I think so. I never heard of the Chaos Dragon... but after you revealed your identity, I seem to recall something."
Kent looked at the rest of his legion. "Any new memories?" They all started looking through their memories... A few minutes later, Zharkaz, the dragon general, widened his eyes.
"I have new memories too," he said, looking both shocked and happy.
"Me too," Kazarak also said.
"I also have new memories," Vorthar, the demon lord, added.
Kent smiled slightly, watching their happy expressions. Though not all of them had regained anything yet, Kent knew it was only a matter of time before they began to recover more of their memories.
Just knowing his true identity had already triggered more memories than what happened after he told them more about his past lives.
’That will certainly trigger more memories, but it is also dangerous. It is not everything I can say... else I might end up destroying them instead of helping them.’
But he was happy for them. However, he will be holding back on revealing his numerous identities for now.
"Zharkaz, what new memories do you have?" Kent asked, looking at the dragon general.
It wasn’t too shocking that someone like Zharkaz would know about a once legendary dragon who lived and made a name for himself.
After all, the Chaos Dragon was also a dragon, and dragons are known to preserve their lineage. Since they like to brag, knowing their ancestors is also beneficial to them.
"The new memories are of me listening to a history of dragons from one of my ancestors. It turns out that during the Primordial Era, the Chaos Dragon was known for its impartiality.

He didn’t discriminate, and aside from being the strongest, he also protected the weak from immortals and gods. He said the Chaos Dragon even preferred to wear his human skin most of the time, since he liked humans more than us dragons.
But can you blame him? I mean, we dragons don’t have a track record for being the most polite, so his decision to live among humans sounds right to me.
Actually, he is my idol of some kind," Zharkaz ended his sentence with an embarrassed expression.
However, he was happy that his idol was now his master... even if he was but a core formation expert at the moment.
Kent looked at him and smiled. ’I know that bastard chose the humans because of the human friend he made... what was her name again... Elina.’
Kent smiled weakly. He knew, even without recalling more of his Chaos memories, that unless Elina made the move, Chaos would never know she had feelings for him.
The Chaos Dragon was indeed known for his strength, but when it came to matters of the heart, he was not too bright.
After reviewing the two pieces of his memories, he saw that most of the ladies in Lumen were interested in Chaos, but he had no idea.
He took their blushing expressions as a sign of fear—fear of him—so he stayed away. And since his presence wasn’t exactly calming, the ladies all decided to admire him from a distance.
Kent just smiled and then turned to the Beast Warden...
"What about you, Kazarak?" Kent asked...
"Mine is a little embarrassing, but I was after a skill created by the Chaos Dragon. A few friends and I ventured into an ancient ruin that appeared all of a sudden...

We entered because, according to those who managed to survive, it is claimed it was from the Primordial Era, and that in a certain dangerous section of this ancient ruin, there was a temple built by the Chaos Dragon that offers skills if you manage to pass a test in the Chaos Temple.
We were eager to enter this temple until we discovered its uniqueness.
It turns out that not even immortals manage to pass the tests, and the shocking part is that the temple was created when the Chaos Dragon wasn’t even an immortal.
I chickened out, so I didn’t even enter the temple. My friends who entered never came out."
Kent shook his head. "Sorry for your loss."
"No, it’s fine. This is the path of cultivation, so such things are bound to happen. Only the strong survive... I guess."
"Still, sorry... And don’t worry, when I start recalling some skills, I will compensate you for your loss." Kazarak smiled, causing Zharkaz to also ask for some.
"I will, but for now, let’s hear what Vorthar has to say."
The demon lord smiled slightly when everyone turned toward him. "I guess I can’t hide it, huh... I think the Chaos Dragon was the reason why I died... well, a piece of his scale was."

Not even a single sound was made when Vorthar spoke. They all clearly heard what he had just said, and that alone made them smile weakly... especially Kent, who could see that Vorthar was also smiling.
"It turns out the Chaos Dragon was and still is someone who is loved by all... everything about him is valuable, down to a piece of his scale."

’That will certainly trigger more memories, but it is also dangerous.
It is not everything I can say... else I might end up destroying them instead of helping them.’
But he was happy for them.
However, he will be holding back on revealing his numerous identities for now.
"Zharkaz, what new memories do you have?" Kent asked, looking at the dragon general.
It wasn’t too shocking that someone like Zharkaz would know about a once legendary dragon who lived and made a name for himself.
After all, the Chaos Dragon was also a dragon, and dragons are known to preserve their lineage.
Since they like to brag, knowing their ancestors is also beneficial to them.
"The new memories are of me listening to a history of dragons from one of my ancestors.
It turns out that during the Primordial Era, the Chaos Dragon was known for its impartiality.
He didn’t discriminate, and aside from being the strongest, he also protected the weak from immortals and gods.
He said the Chaos Dragon even preferred to wear his human skin most of the time, since he liked humans more than us dragons.
But can you blame him?
I mean, we dragons don’t have a track record for being the most polite, so his decision to live among humans sounds right to me.
Actually, he is my idol of some kind," Zharkaz ended his sentence with an embarrassed expression.
However, he was happy that his idol was now his master... even if he was but a core formation expert at the moment.
Kent looked at him and smiled. ’I know that bastard chose the humans because of the human friend he made... what was her name again...
Elina.’
Kent smiled weakly.
He knew, even without recalling more of his Chaos memories, that unless Elina made the move, Chaos would never know she had feelings for him.
The Chaos Dragon was indeed known for his strength, but when it came to matters of the heart, he was not too bright.
After reviewing the two pieces of his memories, he saw that most of the ladies in Lumen were interested in Chaos, but he had no idea.
He took their blushing expressions as a sign of fear—fear of him—so he stayed away.
And since his presence wasn’t exactly calming, the ladies all decided to admire him from a distance.
Kent just smiled and then turned to the Beast Warden...
"What about you, Kazarak?" Kent asked...
"Mine is a little embarrassing, but I was after a skill created by the Chaos Dragon.
A few friends and I ventured into an ancient ruin that appeared all of a sudden...

We entered because, according to those who managed to survive, it is claimed it was from the Primordial Era, and that in a certain dangerous section of this ancient ruin, there was a temple built by the Chaos Dragon that offers skills if you manage to pass a test in the Chaos Temple.
We were eager to enter this temple until we discovered its uniqueness.
It turns out that not even immortals manage to pass the tests, and the shocking part is that the temple was created when the Chaos Dragon wasn’t even an immortal.
I chickened out, so I didn’t even enter the temple.
My friends who entered never came out."
Kent shook his head.
"Sorry for your loss."
"No, it’s fine.
This is the path of cultivation, so such things are bound to happen.
Only the strong survive...
I guess."
"Still, sorry...
And don’t worry, when I start recalling some skills, I will compensate you for your loss." Kazarak smiled, causing Zharkaz to also ask for some.
"I will, but for now, let’s hear what Vorthar has to say."
The demon lord smiled slightly when everyone turned toward him.
"I guess I can’t hide it, huh...
I think the Chaos Dragon was the reason why I died... well, a piece of his scale was."
Not even a single sound was made when Vorthar spoke.
They all clearly heard what he had just said, and that alone made them smile weakly... especially Kent, who could see that Vorthar was also smiling.
"It turns out the Chaos Dragon was and still is someone who is loved by all... everything about him is valuable, down to a piece of his scale."

chapters.title: Chapter 677: The Way Forward [Bonus]
paragraphs: Vorthar had already retrieved a memory that showed he was betrayed by his wives and the Demon King he served under. It was a brutal betrayal, considering he said wives, not wife.
It was a common thread he shared with the Barbarian King Gorzak, who was also betrayed.
So the dark pill of betrayal had already left its bitter mark in his mouth. He knew he had been betrayed, but he had no idea how it had happened.
But now he does...
...and the answer isn’t one he expected—none of them expected that.
"It turns out I ventured into an ancient ruin full of perils but returned triumphantly with the scale of the Primordial Chaos Dragon...
It was my one shot at becoming someone worthy of being equal to a Demon King. But it turns out I wasn’t meant to be... I didn’t even get to celebrate my achievement with everyone."
Vorthar clenched his fist, recalling the fateful day he returned to see his wife in the arms of the Demon King and his death smiling at him in the face. That was a bitter poison to swallow.
His friends could tell he was seething with anger, and judging by the aura emanating from him, they knew that the day he would arrive in his world, all hell would break loose.
Kent sighed in his heart and then tapped into his connection with Yi Lai, who was on her way to the oracle headquarters to kill every last one of them.

’Yi La, leave one of the oracles alive and tell them to deliver a message to the Hand for me. Tell them I said they should hurry, or else I will make them do it painfully. They have less than three years to open the gate of the apocalypse.’

His message was simple: since the apocalypse is bound to come, he must have a timeline. After all, his two reasons for staying and facing the apocalypse were that he wanted to save the world his journey began in, and also preserve the world his wives were born in.
He wasn’t planning to leave Sonox for another five years, perhaps more. This was because Gaia stated that only from the Pill King stage can one register as an Alchemist in the high worlds.
Naturally, Kent knew there would be a way to navigate that, but since he had nothing to rush into, he planned to become a Pill King before moving to a High World.
But his chaotic blood was boiling now for revenge. Hearing what happened to Vorthar, he wanted to rise through the ranks faster and help him get his revenge.
So he wanted things in Sonox to escalate.

Right now, he didn’t even want to figure out why the Hand was planning on opening the gate of apocalypse. He just wanted it to open, and once it closed, there would be no way to reopen it ever again...
This meant the Hand was being too slow.

They had already found four keys; they were left with only three... so Kent wanted them to hurry, and after what Yi Lai planned to do at the Oracle headquarters, the Hand would start to take him seriously.
"Don’t worry, Vorthar, we will get your revenge, and now that you are my subordinate, I will ensure you know more about me, that goes to you all...
When the time comes, the entire universe will recognize you all as friends and family of the Chaos Dragon..."
They all laughed, and deep inside, they were happy.
Especially Zharkaz, who couldn’t wait to brag about his status once his memories returned. Kent knew that this arrogant dragon needed to be brought down a peg or else his arrogance would be his doom.
But for now, he would let him have his moment.
Kent spent a few more hours with his legion, sparring with them.

Naturally, he won all the spars the moment he used his bloodline. He made them all use at least 10% of the bloodline since he had no reason to see their wrecked selves after every spar, like he did with Kaizo.
Ultimately, they suffered a devastating defeat. Kent even wondered if he was truly only using 1% of his bloodline, but in the end, that was the only answer... even the tower confirmed it.
After the sparring session, which they all enjoyed, he left and went back to the Soul Tower to examine a few things.

First, he tried to use more of his bloodline, but he was met with severe pain that caused him to black out. When he woke up five days later, a severe headache rocked his brain, telling him not to be stupid ever again.
Naturally, he took that warning to heart.

"So the only way to surpass 1% is to cultivate the Primal Bone Tempering Art," Kent said, looking at his arm covered in dragon scales. "But the only way to cultivate it is through bloodshed. However, I can’t stay for long inside the dungeon since I have to seek out the Pill Princess."

Kent fell and lay on his back, staring at the blue sky and thirteen moons. Three shone more brightly than the other ten. He paid little attention to them since his focus was drawn back to the issue at hand.

"I have two months left to get to the Half-Elves Kingdom, which means I have less than sixty days on the outside to at least master the first form." Kent thought for a moment, then a smirk appeared on his lips.
"Not that I have to be afraid of anyone out there. This is a medium world, and my strength is enough to put me at the peak... but being too powerful isn’t bad either."
Kent rose from his comfortable state and sat down. He then decided to learn the Primal Bone Tempering Art.
This way, while he was away, every small kill would benefit him. He is venturing into a pool of people...some stupid ones would try to court death...

"Then again, I can just use the dungeons in here to master at least the first form. It took Chaos several years, but with the no-dying policy in the dungeons, I can master the first form much faster...
⟦Unfortunately, the master can’t use the dungeons to cultivate the Primal Bone Tempering Art. It can only be practiced in a life-and-death battle.⟧
A weak smile appeared on Kent’s face... ’Why did I even think it would be that easy?’
He closed his eyes, a smile playing on his lips as he dove into comprehending the Primal Bone Tempering Art...
A few minutes later, his consciousness was pulled into a world of blood...

chapters.title: Chapter 678: Giant Red Door
paragraphs: When Chaos learned the Primal Bone Tempering Art, Kent only felt what it was like to learn the technique. So, he never truly knew what happened during the learning process..
That was why he was taken aback when he was pulled into a world he could only describe as horrific. He was standing in water that reached his waist.
He had no idea how vast it was, but from what he could see, it resembled a river, given its vastness and encompassing nature.
The water was red, and while it didn’t have the feel of blood, it carried its stench—the metallic stench of blood was palpable in the water.
The air was filled with it, and as he looked at the red sky and red sun—or perhaps the moon—Kent knew he had found himself in yet another freaky situation.
This time, instead of a large dragon swinging its claws downward, Kent found himself in a much more dire situation.
The water was not blood, so there is a bonus to that...
However, it came with its disadvantages, and one of them was the fact that Kent was already losing his spiritual qi, not rapidly, but at a rate that would drain him if he remained there for long.

So he spread his senses across the space to look for a way out. However, no matter where he looked, all he saw was the vastness of red water. There was no sense of direction. It was essentially water, and he appeared to be standing in the middle.

This meant that if he moved forward, he didn’t know if it would take him to his destination or if he should move back. It didn’t have any heads or tails to it. But he had to do something, or else he would run out of energy, and who knows what would happen then.
He most certainly wouldn’t want to find out the hard way...
So he knew he had to pick a direction.
"A wise man once said, the first thought that comes to mind is often right... Backwards then." Kent turned around and began moving toward the direction his back had initially faced.
He knew he had to move, so he chose a direction and began to move. The rest would depend on whether his choice led him to where he wanted to go.
Hours passed, and all Kent could do was keep moving. And while his leg was touching the floor of this great red river, it didn’t feel like he was moving any faster.

He was walking, which was less taxing compared to swinging his arms and legs. Swimming that way would consume more energy, unlike walking, which consumed relatively little. But despite that, he wasn’t moving any faster or approaching his destination.
If there was even a destination to get to.
For all he knew, this was just an aimless walk that held no meaning...

But he couldn’t stop now, especially since he didn’t know how to get out of the damn river or the wierd space he had found himself in. He couldn’t communicate with the Tower, nor could he reach out to his three assistants.
It was as if his connection to all who could help him was severed. Of course, Gaia told him this might happen often...

She explained that there are many laws in the universe, some of which are stricter than others. So in most cases, some worlds would have laws that prevented him from doing things like talking telepathically to his wives—the three of them—or even the tower.

It is more common for him to experience this in high worlds. However, he had already started to experience it now, which showed that his tower was powerful, but there were laws even it couldn’t break or dare to break in order to maintain balance...

If it could break any laws, then Kent wouldn’t have to do anything. The tower could basically raise his cultivation base, master alchemy for him, learn the laws for him, and even allow him to kill gods without having much strength.
The laws govern everything. They govern the various stages in cultivation, the energies one uses in combat, or even the skills used in combat.

If the tower can break said laws, then Kent wouldn’t even have to do anything...He can command a Celestial to drop dead, and since the laws that regulate that command are broken, the Celestial will indeed drop dead.
That will be a disaster...

Of course, the tower could help him gain access to more information, give him powerful gifts, and other valuable things, but that didn’t mean it could break the laws and allow him, a core formation expert, to kill a god.
That is not something that has a happy ending...
So, Kent knew he had to sometimes chase after what he wanted, using his strength and will. This way, he wouldn’t rely solely on the tower.

And today, he found himself in a situation that made him miss the tower and his three assistants. But that didn’t change the fact that he still didn’t know where he was going or what he was meant to do.
He was moving in a direction he had picked on a whim, and that alone shows he was just going along, while deep down, he hoped he had chosen the right direction to take.
In simple terms, he had no sense of direction in the Great Red River.
A day passed, and he could only continue to move. Eventually, he started to notice a change. He began to lose more energy than before, and the water grew stronger, resisting him even further.
Kent cursed but continued to move. Eventually, the pressure in the river grew even stronger, slowing down his movement considerably.
It was like he couldn’t even move his legs a couple of inches without feeling the pressure pushing back.
"At this rate, I will need years to get to my destination, even if there is one," Kent sighed and then kept moving. Eventually, he started to take a few more seconds before he could move his leg.

"No wonder Chaos took five years just to learn this technique," Kent smirked. "Why am I even complaining... the reward is something I will enjoy greatly. I know Chaos did." Kent smiled, then kept moving.
Eventually, he caught sight of something in the far distance. It was far away—very far away. However, he saw something, and that thing was what he was after.
So Kent started moving toward it. It was slow and would probably take weeks to reach, but he kept moving regardless.
Granted, he reached his destination; whatever awaited him would be taken care of. Chaos was able to do it, so he most certainly would have to do it.
Not that he was comparing himself to the freak, but he most certainly wanted to surpass himself...His mentor is himself, and he plans to surpass himself.
The resistance in the water continued to increase as he moved. It took him hours to move a couple of meters, even half a dozen meters. But Kent was moving forward nonetheless.
Eventually, the structure he saw became clearer as he got closer... after days, perhaps weeks—Kent lost count—but after a while, he came within 100 meters of a giant red door.
"Well, that just looks terrifying."

chapters.title: Chapter 679: Writings on A Door
paragraphs: The door towered several meters tall, supported by metallic frames that, judging by their appearance, were not ordinary metal.
They look like frames supporting the gate of hell. They are imposing and well, just terrifying...
Then again, considering the drawings on it weren’t languages the ordinary eye could see and the ordinary mind could read, it was clear the door was no simple door.
It looked imposing and dripped with red energy. Though the main door was deep black, the reddish energy emitting from it made it look horrific...
Kent looked up and saw that a large chain bound the door, so opening it wasn’t going to be easy.
He relaxed his muscles and decided to look at it carefully...

When he had seen enough or as much as he could from afar, he gradually began to move toward it. It took considerable time, but eventually, he came close to the towering door and stepped onto land for the first time in perhaps months.
The moment he stepped on land, he felt his body free of all the resistance the water had put him through. He felt he had become even stronger as a result, and his drained energy had even returned.
’It feels good to have my energy back at least...
He raised his head and looked at the door. Now that he was closer, he saw that the door was situated on a stairway with seven steps.
And the door itself, now that he was closer, looked imposing. The door, as he noticed, was deep black, and judging by its rough surface, the metal would be heavy and very durable.

"I mean, I just have to get close and see if I can get this over with... touching it will reveal what I have to do next." Kent stepped on the first step... slowly at first, since he was familiar with most stairways.
He had one in his tower after all.
’Ordinary Stairway, huh...’
Thankfully, there was no pressure on it, so he quickly climbed it.

He stopped in front of the towering door, and then a deep sigh escaped his mouth. He was like a pebble in front of the large door. Of course, he didn’t think too much about it and decided to check what he had to do.
He placed his palm on the door, expecting to hear a voice or get the info in his head. However, nothing of the sort happened.
Kent frowned. "Mostly, that is how these things are done. I put my hand on the door, and I will be informed on how to proceed. So what went wrong?"
He placed his left palm on the door again, but still nothing happened. This prompted Kent to enter a contemplative state, pondering what he was doing wrong.
After a few more minutes, a sigh escaped his lips.
"I guess I am so used to my human form that I am forgetting I am a dragon." Kent activated his Chaos dragon bloodline, and to his shock, the space he was in shook as if it was welcoming him.
The red river shook, and even the stairway shone brightly when his bloodline was activated.
"That’s more like it," Kent grinned, then placed his palm on the door. This time, he heard a humming sound spread from beneath his palm and wash over the door.
Suddenly, the surface of the door became smooth. However, the large chain still bound it in the middle. While that made Kent frown, a smile appeared on his face because now he knew what he had to do.
"So I must break the chain with my fist... and then open the door." Kent smiled weakly, knowing neither of the two tasks was as simple as it sounded.
Just looking at the enormous chains binding the door was enough for Kent to know he was out of his league. But he also needed the technique, so he had to break it.

However, Chaos had done it, so he knew he could do it too. "Since I am the same person as Chaos, why can’t I just learn the technique without having to go through all this?"
He managed to learn the Transcendent Heavenly Sword technique by just experiencing Jest’s memories, so why couldn’t he do the same with Chaos’s memory?
A sigh escaped Kent’s mouth.

I didn’t lose count; this is proof I am better than you if you are reading this.

chapters.title: Chapter 680: Making a Decision [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent stood before the imposing gate with a smirk on his face.
"Did I just get fucked over by my own incarnation..." Obviously, the answer was obvious. Chaos had indeed played a good sport on him, and the outcome was Kent cursing himself.
Which was ironic, considering he never truly expected anything different. He would have done the same thing if he were in Chaos’ place...
’But wait...Chaos and I are the same person...so it means I wasnt in my place and I choose to fuck up the peaceful life of my future self’ Kent smiled weakily...
’Was I this crazy in all my incarnations...’ He shuddered thinking about it.
’If the answer is yes...then it means I am going to suffer 13 times over..."
"Fuck Me..." Kent broke down thinking about his life...and the path her had set for himself...one he cant dare not to traverse.
"...From the moment I met that guy, I knew he had a few screws loose in his head... who would have thought those screws would make him mess this hard with me?"
Kent sighed, and then a smile appeared on his face. "Looks like I am not destined to learn this technique today."

He indeed could not learn the technique. The reason was that the last few words Chaos left him. It appeared that before he could break the chain, he had to learn a different type of aura called [Blood Aura] and then merge it with the Chaos Claw Aura.
Kent had already awakened the Chaos Claw Aura, so he was left with the Blood Aura. However, judging from what Chaos left him, he was fucked either way.
Not that he expected anything different from someone like Chaos, but he never expected his incarnation to be this unruly.

"This can only mean one thing: this place is a physical space, and so what Chaos wrote here is still here waiting for me as if he knew he would one day come back here." Kent sighed and then started flying up.
"Before I make a decision, I must at least know what happened to him. Thankfully, Chaos had time to document his journey from the day he arrived in front of this door."
It took Kent a few minutes, but he managed to locate the first day of Chaos’s arrival...
⟦Day 1: So I am officially in the realm of Chaos and Blood. The name is a little on the nose, but I had to get things moving, so accept what you got.
The Blood Sea was a headache, but I managed to get to the door in one piece. Now I just have to shatter this damn chain and I will be out of here.
I know it won’t be easy, but I am not an easy dragon, too... I wasn’t called Chaos for nothing...
Actually, I gave myself that name, but then again, I don’t think there will ever be a name better than mine... Imagine growing up among immortals with a name like Kent... I mean, come on.⟧

"It is official... I was an idiot, a sadistic, manipulative, evil person in my first life. I mean, what kind of idiot was I to think now is the best time to joke about the name I will go by in my future life?" Kent looked at the writing for a few more seconds, and a sigh escaped his lips.
"I guess I knew I would be coming here one day, so I left myself a couple of messages, if only the messages were more important." A smile appeared on Kent’s lips as he shifted to the second day...
⟦Day 2: So it turns out that if you don’t want every bone in your body to shatter, never attempt to break the chain... I learned it the hard way.
Also, the healing process is significantly slower here, so you might want to avoid getting injured. Then again, you can try and see if you are luckier than I.⟧
"No, thank you... I trust myself well enough not to attempt this disastrous enterprise," Kent smiled and then looked toward the rest of the writings for day 2.
Secretly, though, he was happy Chaos suffered when he tried to break the chain...
⟦I need to think of a way out. Although I can probably stay here for a few more months, I need to resolve this issue soon, and the only way to do that is to find a solution.
The first thought that came to mind was using a martial technique, but then I found out I don’t have a martial technique. But even if I do, I don’t think it would have worked.

So the only way now is to strengthen my fist, and perhaps that will help me break this damn chain. I have a few ideas, and one is to train my Chaos Claw Aura. I know it is a long shot, but that will do.⟧
"Evil and sadistic, but he left some insightful messages here for me to add to my experience of his life." The memories inscribed on the walls are not in the memory he unlocked using the memory keys.
This means that within this realm, the memory cannot be extracted using a memory key. Kent had already lived past this point of Chaos’s memories, but he had never seen these portions of his memories.
So this is a new experience for him.

The only downside here is that he would have to do everything by himself instead of inheriting it from Chaos. It doesn’t sound too bad... "However, I don’t have time to get into things now. So I have to go back and come later," Kent sighed.
He looked around the door and saw more writings.
If he were to get into it now, things would become much more immersive, and he might remain there for years.
Thankfully, there was something he noticed about the tower: whenever he entered a strange state, time seemed to continue running based on the tower’s time, so there was at least a silver lining.
It means months passed, but on the outside, it was a few days...But he can’t afford to stay here for long...
He flew down and landed softly on the ground.

"I will come back, and perhaps next time, I will learn more about this Maw of the Abyss. The name sounds ominous, and so I have no doubt it will be a harrowing adversary." Kent sat down and then willed himself to leave the space he was in...
The next second, he opened his eyes inside the tower. However, the moment he did, his Chaos Claw Aura surged, becoming much stronger than before.
It felt like just remaining in the Realm of Blood and Chaos was not entirely wasted. His Chaos Claw has become more powerful...
He didn’t use it during his spar with Kaizo, and it was probably for the best. Kaizo would have died if he used it...
"I’d better get my affairs in order and get back there fast. Perhaps next time, I will be walking out with something good."
Kent checked with the tower and realized he had been away for two and a half months. "This means the dungeon has finished upgrading."
Kent quickly checked the messages he had received and located the one meant for the dungeon...
⟦Your quest ’Shadow Guardian of Planet Dusk’ has undergone some changes⟧

chapters.title: Chapter 681: First Hell Rank Quest [Bonus]
paragraphs: ⟦Your quest ’Shadow Guardian of Planet Dusk’ has undergone some changes⟧
⟦The dungeon has been upgraded from SSS ↠ Unique⟧
⟦Number of floors upgraded from 32 ↠ 37⟧
⟦The difficulty of the dungeon has been upgraded from Calamity ↠ Hell⟧

"Well, things just took a dark turn," Kent said weakly. He had a year and a couple of months that he could have used to complete the original quest when he emerged from his sword and draconic enlightenments while in seclusion.

He and the ladies alongside his legion could have used that time to enter the dungeon and clear every last floor within months. However, a message was waiting for him when he came out of his second draconic enlightenment.
The message read...
⟦Quest Message: An unknown anomaly has occurred, which triggered the Dusk Dungeon to enter an upgrade process. Time till completion: 12,418 days⟧
That was the message, if Kent recalls correctly. The time was estimated based on the tower time, so Kent knew he still had some time.
He doesn’t know what triggered the anomaly, but he knows there is nothing good about anomalies. He is an anomaly, and so far, he has seen how wicked he can be to himself.
That alone pisses him off.
But now, this dungeon has moved from being SSS to a Unique dungeon where even gods can be waiting for them in there.

After all, it is a unique dungeon, and as such, the limit that is placed on other dungeons has been lifted. Kent didn’t know if this was a blessing in disguise or if he was going to submerge himself, his wives, and his legion in a literal hell.
But one thing is sure: he is fucked either way. A unique dungeon isn’t something to be taken lightly... They are rare, and Kent had just found himself in one...
⟦Quest Name: Shadow Guardian of Planet Dusk⟧
⟦Quest Type: World Quest⟧
⟦Quest Difficulty: Hell⟧
→ The war between the brave warriors of Planet Dusk and the Evil Ant Queen Elxn of Planet Kuynx happened 15,000 years ago. It was a grave battle that resulted in the deaths of billions of Duskins.

→ They lost 90% of their warriors and 60% of the entire race. They lost their planet protector in that fateful battle, considering she chose to use her life to end it all. She couldn’t afford to survive while everyone else died around her.
→ Her ultimate sacrifice saved billions more and a few warriors who would lead the people of Dusk to a new age.

→ But while the battle ended, the war didn’t. The planet-killing dungeon that the Ant Queen had prepared 2,000 years in advance was planted in the world of Dusk, her last-ditch effort to eradicate the loyal followers of the Goddess of Love.

→ But the universe, being touched by the loyalty of the Duskians, intervened and placed a limit on the Planet Killer, turning it into a dungeon that, for the past 12,000 years, has been spawning beasts of all kinds.
→ It was the most straightforward way to contain them since the universe is powerless to eradicate them.

→ But 7,500 years ago, the dungeon had reached its maximum threshold, and so the seal around it started to weaken. When it finally breaks, the dungeon will open, and millions of horrors will be revealed.
→ However, before that could happen, something intervened, and so the dungeon remained sealed until now.
→ The anomaly that happened caused the Planet Dungeon to undergo some drastic changes, turning the planet-killer dungeon from SSS rank to a Unique one.
⟦Changes: The parameters of the dungeon have changed. You now have 12 years to rise through the 37 levels/floors and kill the Ant King Ketu, who was biding his time until the ritual is performed.
The moment the ritual is performed, he will be unleashed upon the world of Dusk. Allowing that to happen will come with severe consequences, ones you don’t want to face.
No respawns for both the dungeon creatures and you.⟧

⟦Lore: There are many secrets in the dungeon, secrets that will bring changes to the World of Dusk, you, your wives, and your legion. These secrets come in the form of drops after major kills. Uncover them all.⟧
→ Details of the Planet Killer Dungeon
⟦Name: Planet Killer Dungeon⟧
⟦Grade: Unique⟧
⟦Floors/Levels: 37⟧
⟦Power Levels: Peak Core Formation - Unknown⟧
There will be rewards for clearing every level; however, the overall rewards are listed below after completing the entire quest. Hidden rewards will be revealed after the quest is completed.
⟪Rewards:⟫
→ 100 Billion Tower Points
→ True Name Tokens (20)
→ Ten Destiny Memory Keys (Unity)
→ True Name Memory Keys (Unknown Quantity)
→ Thirty Memory Keys (7 different Incarnations)
→ Ascension Platform (Immortal grade)
→ Planet Dusk Upgrade Key
→ Hidden Rewards (Twenty)
"This is just something else. Even the base power level is at the peak of the core formation stage. This is going to be more harrowing than even the battle that will soon happen in Fedora."
Kent smiled weakly.
"Tower, can you estimate the number of creatures to clear on the first floor?" Kent asked. It used to be 32 floors, now it is 37... This means things won’t be as simple as before.
⟦I can’t precisely estimate... However, expect not less than 1,000 creatures. Additionally, there is a possibility that not all creatures will be at the Core Formation stage.⟧
"I see. This means there might be Spirit Ascension stage creatures waiting for us, or even those at a higher level."
⟦Most likely.⟧
"I see. Thank you, Tower." Kent stood up and stretched his muscles. "The legion and the girls will handle the first few floors... I need to get my affairs in order before joining them."

Kent didn’t want to admit it, but he was excited to embark on such a long-term quest. It was going to be dangerous, but the moment he ascends to a High World, and his ladies start to rise in their ranks, things will be much more manageable.
He walked toward a certain tree and then plucked a ripe mango. Naturally, it was a spirit mango, one that nourishes the soul and enhances its essence.
He bit into it and started eating...
After he finished consuming the mango, Kent left the Soul Tower and went to the mountain garden. He wanted to meet Gaia and her sisters and play with them, just as he had promised.
The moment he goes away this time, it will be several years before they can play together. When he appeared in the garden, his eyes landed on them.
However, to Kent’s surprise, the fourth Loli was there too, and she spotted him first.
"Big brother, I miss you so much." Li Hua ran and jumped into his arms, planting her face into his chest.

→ Her ultimate sacrifice saved billions more and a few warriors who would lead the people of Dusk to a new age.
→ But while the battle ended, the war didn’t.
The planet-killing dungeon that the Ant Queen had prepared 2,000 years in advance was planted in the world of Dusk, her last-ditch effort to eradicate the loyal followers of the Goddess of Love.

→ But the universe, being touched by the loyalty of the Duskians, intervened and placed a limit on the Planet Killer, turning it into a dungeon that, for the past 12,000 years, has been spawning beasts of all kinds.
→ It was the most straightforward way to contain them since the universe is powerless to eradicate them.
→ But 7,500 years ago, the dungeon had reached its maximum threshold, and so the seal around it started to weaken.
When it finally breaks, the dungeon will open, and millions of horrors will be revealed.
→ However, before that could happen, something intervened, and so the dungeon remained sealed until now.
→ The anomaly that happened caused the Planet Dungeon to undergo some drastic changes, turning the planet-killer dungeon from SSS rank to a Unique one.
⟦Changes: The parameters of the dungeon have changed.
You now have 12 years to rise through the 37 levels/floors and kill the Ant King Ketu, who was biding his time until the ritual is performed.
The moment the ritual is performed, he will be unleashed upon the world of Dusk.
Allowing that to happen will come with severe consequences, ones you don’t want to face.
No respawns for both the dungeon creatures and you.⟧
⟦Lore: There are many secrets in the dungeon, secrets that will bring changes to the World of Dusk, you, your wives, and your legion.
These secrets come in the form of drops after major kills.
Uncover them all.⟧
→ Details of the Planet Killer Dungeon
⟦Name: Planet Killer Dungeon⟧
⟦Grade: Unique⟧
⟦Floors/Levels: 37⟧
⟦Power Levels: Peak Core Formation - Unknown⟧
There will be rewards for clearing every level; however, the overall rewards are listed below after completing the entire quest.
Hidden rewards will be revealed after the quest is completed.
⟪Rewards:⟫
→ 100 Billion Tower Points
→ True Name Tokens (20)
→ Ten Destiny Memory Keys (Unity)
→ True Name Memory Keys (Unknown Quantity)
→ Thirty Memory Keys (7 different Incarnations)
→ Ascension Platform (Immortal grade)
→ Planet Dusk Upgrade Key
→ Hidden Rewards (Twenty)
"This is just something else.
Even the base power level is at the peak of the core formation stage.
This is going to be more harrowing than even the battle that will soon happen in Fedora."
Kent smiled weakly.
"Tower, can you estimate the number of creatures to clear on the first floor?" Kent asked.
It used to be 32 floors, now it is 37...
This means things won’t be as simple as before.
⟦I can’t precisely estimate...
However, expect not less than 1,000 creatures.
Additionally, there is a possibility that not all creatures will be at the Core Formation stage.⟧
"I see.
This means there might be Spirit Ascension stage creatures waiting for us, or even those at a higher level."
⟦Most likely.⟧
"I see.
Thank you, Tower." Kent stood up and stretched his muscles.
"The legion and the girls will handle the first few floors...
I need to get my affairs in order before joining them."
Kent didn’t want to admit it, but he was excited to embark on such a long-term quest.
It was going to be dangerous, but the moment he ascends to a High World, and his ladies start to rise in their ranks, things will be much more manageable.
He walked toward a certain tree and then plucked a ripe mango.
Naturally, it was a spirit mango, one that nourishes the soul and enhances its essence.
He bit into it and started eating...
After he finished consuming the mango, Kent left the Soul Tower and went to the mountain garden.
He wanted to meet Gaia and her sisters and play with them, just as he had promised.
The moment he goes away this time, it will be several years before they can play together.
When he appeared in the garden, his eyes landed on them.
However, to Kent’s surprise, the fourth Loli was there too, and she spotted him first.
"Big brother, I miss you so much." Li Hua ran and jumped into his arms, planting her face into his chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 682: Li Hua’s Shocking Reveal [Bonus]
paragraphs: "Li Hua, you have become bigger since the last time I saw you," Kent said, brushing his hand against Li Hua’s back. The small human he rescued years ago has grown significantly.
Of course, she is bigger hypothetically...A loli will always remain a Loli.
However, she is 15 years and a few months old, which means she was nearing her coming-of-age period when her meridians would mature enough, allowing her to harness spiritual qi.

"I miss you, big brother...I have a lot of things to tell you and show you, but Gaia said you were busy, so I have been waiting for you." Li Hua said happily now that she gets to talk to her big brother.
Kent was also happy.
Li Hua had been preparing hard for when she would start cultivating, and looking at her now, he knew she had made some huge progress.
He felt a little guilty that he wasn’t around often to play with her. But now he gets to play with her...
"Let’s sit down first," Kent said, carrying her to the edge of the mountain and then stepping into a flying boat. The sun is almost set, so the horizon looks beautiful.

The moment Kent landed in the boat, Akira, Gaia, and Dori surrounded him. Looking at the three troublemakers seated with Li Hua, Kent knew it was only a matter of time before Li Hua joined them to torment him.
The flying boat started drifting through the air, moving over the beautiful city below.
"Well then, Li Hua, why dont you tell me what you wanted to say so badly?" The Atomic beauty smiled, and she extended her hand, forming a black flame.
Kent’s eyes widened as she looked at the black flame twirling in her hands. "Is that a soul flame?" Kent asked, looking closely at the black flame.

"Yes," Both Li Hua and the Three cosmic Lolis answered with smiles on their faces. Kent studied the flame for a few seconds and then turned to look at Li Hua, whose face had already started to turn pale.
"That will be enough, Li Hua." She put away the flame and smiled at Kent.
"How?" Kent asked, looking at Li Hua and the three Lolis beside her.

"When I was meditating, I blacked out and appeared in a deep forest where everything is black. Even the sun was black...I was scared. However, just when I started to panic, a small rabbit appeared before me and started to play with me.
I stayed there for a long time, and when it was time for the rabbit to leave, she gave me the flame and said we would meet again... that when the time was right, she would come to seek me out.
"To do what?" Kent asked.
Li Hua shook her head, "I dont know...But I hope she comes faster...Pauli was a good girl."
"Pauli?"

"Yes...That was her name. She said she is from a very far place...I just played with her mostly, so a lot of the things she said I don’t recall...but she was my best friend, so I will train hard and wait for her to come find me."
Kent was puzzled, bewildered even...
All Li Hua just said sounded like fiction to him, but yet again, the evidence was there, and it was a form of black flame... So, if that was the case, then how did she manage to gain enlightenment?
The moment a person gains enlightenment, their consciousness will be drawn into the realm of enlightenment, leaving their body behind.

However, while their body remain on the outside, that doesn’t mean they are dead. Their soul leaving their body means death...the only reason one remains alive is if they have enough spiritual Qi to keep their bodies warm.
Which is why Li Hua attaining enlightenment at this stage isn’t plausible...it shouldn’t have been possible because she can’t channel spiritual qi...
But looking at how she was able to light a soul flame... There was no other explanation aside from enlightenment.

’But she is just 15 and a few months old...However, to be able to use spiritual Qi, she must be at least 16 years old, not a day younger. So, then why was she able to gain enlightenment? And from the way she said it, it sounded like she had remained in the enlightenment for a very long time.’
Kent’s mind is reeling.
"Any explanations as to how she was able to attain enlightenment?" Kent asked his three assistants, who were smiling at him, knowing full well what was going on in his head.

⟪First of all, Li Hua is a rare genius. Her potential is endless...just like yours, and while I would love to say she had indeed attained enlightenment, we both know that is impossible...not unless she turns 16.

So, she didn’t attain enlightenment; instead, she was pulled into the realm of darkness - the outer sections. But that was where she went, and that was where she met her best friend Pauli, who gave her the Flames of Darkness.⟫ Dori explained
"The realm of Darkness?" Kent was hit with yet another shocker
⟪The realm of Darkness is the true place where darkness originated. It contains the elemental Law of Darkness, the True Law of Darkness, and the True Form of Darkness.
Only a few have access to it, and Li Hua is one of them. It is a dangerous place, but it is also rich with rewards.
The moment she starts to harness Spiritual energy, her darkness element will awaken, and when it does, she will gain access to the Realm of darkness again, and she can travel there willingly...
Though I will advise against that, considering it is not a place that can be ventured into Casually⟫
"I see. This is good then..." Kent smiled at Li Hua, who held a dagger now in her hand. She flipped it casually through her fingers, spinning it a few times on her palm while she looked at Kent.
Yes, she was showing off her skills to Kent, who just remained puzzled for a couple of minutes. Though she hasn’t yet awakened her Assassin Class, her dagger movement is already impressive.

Gaia. Dori and Akira could only smile, watching the Atomic beauty execute her dagger skills flawlessly. In the end, Kent decided to concoct a couple of Meridian upgrade pills and spiritual Qi enhancement pills for her.
Though she can’t channel Spiritual Qi now, the pills will prepare her for when she finally starts to harness spiritual Qi. It will set her ahead of her peers.

chapters.title: Chapter 683: The Dragon Necromancer’s Revenge (1)
paragraphs: (Ancient Battlefield of Parting - Outer Section)
Slash

Yi Lai slashed her sword downward, beheading a red-fur demon tiger. Beside her, Nethar, her red undead dragon, who was in his humanoid form, sprayed fire from his mouth, burning yet another red-fur demon tiger.

A couple of meters away, Veera had also beheaded another tiger. Looking around, dozens of tigers lay dead, their bodies separated from their heads—some turned to charred remains, showing Nethar was the cause of their death.

When Yi Lai left the tower to get her revenge on the Oracles, she didn’t immediately head there. Instead, she took a detour to the ancient Battlefield of Parting, specifically the domain of the Red Fur Demon Tigers.
The moment they arrived, they were attacked, and thus, for the past few minutes, they had been killing like crazy.

Veera yet again beheaded a tiger—this one had already refined its core three times, showing it was already a powerful one. They were meant to be powerful, but to someone like Veera, they were just weaklings.
She looked toward Yi Lai, who was equally beheading the tigers like it was the most normal thing to do. Veera shook her head and said to Yi Lai,
"Again, why are we doing this? I don’t suppose this is just a kink of yours... and poor me was dragged in."

Yi Lai, who heard Veera’s question, smirked. However, Veera wasn’t done. "You are not exactly the type to raise tigers from the dead, and I know you don’t have an appetite for these weaklings... not even Nethar will fancy their meat.
I know I don’t want them in my Undead Army, too... so why are we killing them?"
Yi Lai stopped and blasted three tigers away using her black lightning. She looked at Veera curiously and sighed. "I guess I wanted revenge so bad that I couldn’t let these idiots go.

Don’t tell the others... I know they will tease me for sure, but when I first arrived in the Ancient Battelfield of Partimg, the Red Fur Demon Tigers ambushed me, and if not for a life-saving treasure, I would have died...or something even worse would have happened to me."
Yi Lai paused and unleashed a powerful attack that cleaved through the body of a tiger, sending both halves of its body tumbling down.
She pointed her finger at another tiger, and a streak of lightning shot out, drawing holes in its head.
"...They were too strong back then... and so, for the hundreds of years I spent here, I tried to get my revenge... but I couldn’t because of the Tiger King.
He had long formed his core and refined it seven times, making him one of the most dangerous beasts in the outer section of this vast battlefield.
Now I have the strength, and I want to kill him... Just see it as me coming for a long-overdue revenge, just like I will get one on the Oracles and then eventually, The Hand."
Veera studied Yi Lai for a few seconds before a smile appeared on her lips. "I understand. I know that revenge is a complex concept, regardless of how people perceive it...
And don’t worry, I won’t say a word to our brothers and sisters..."
"Yes, you would... I can already tell—you told them... because Kaizo told me." Yi Lai smiled weakly and resumed her battle.
"That muscle-headed brute..." Veera cursed and then continued killing more tigers.
A few minutes later, a terrifying pressure descended on the battlefield, causing Yi Lai, Nethar, and Veera to halt their attacks and look toward the new arrival.

It was a human with a muscular body, red hair, and a tiger’s set of eyes. He had gloves with sharp claws, and considering his body density, it wouldn’t be surprising if his strength far surpassed Yi Lai’s.
"You come again, Lady Hunter... I see you brought some friends," the red-haired human said, turning toward Veera and showing his sharp tiger teeth.
"I am King Tyron, but you can call me Tiger King if you want, my lady..." The lust in his eyes was dripping, and Veera could see it.
Yi Lai, who saw Tyron casting lustful eyes on Veera, tightened her grip on her sword and pointed it at him. "You will die today, Tyron... so be prepared."
Tyron smiled. "You are always too bitter, Hunter... All I wanted was for you to become my queen, but you ran. No need to be bitter about that—"
Tyron laughed sadistically and then turned toward Veera. However, before he could say something, Veera raised her slender, tattooed hand and gave him the middle finger.
The tattoo of a bone drawn on her finger glowed purple, and ten Core formation undead swordsmen appeared behind her. Tyron’s smile vanished.
Veera turned to Yi Lai and smiled. "Be sure to make him bleed."

With that, she and her undead swordsmen started killing the weaker tigers while Yi Lai looked toward Tyron. However, she didn’t immediately attack; instead, she put away her sword and channeled her black lightning into a gauntlet.
She wouldn’t feel good if she easily killed the bastard, so it would be done gradually and painfully, as Veera advised.
"Should I back you up, master?" Nether asked, but Yi Lai shook her head.
"I alone will be enough to handle this skirt chaser—" With that, she vanished and appeared before King Tyron, planting her fist in his face.
The punch was enough to shatter stones and bend metal, so it wasn’t surprising when King Tyron heard his jaw crack.

Nethar looked at her master and shook his head. "Master clearly has some anger issues against men. I’d better warn the guys inside the tower not to come close or have any ideas unless they want to become undead like me."
With that, the undead dragon formed a sword from his red flames and started dispatching the weaker tigers.

Veera and her team moved through the battlefield, killing as they advanced. The tigers were no match for them at all. It even felt like bullying, but earning a few tower points for their master wasn’t too bad...
And perhaps a few soul essences to fuel his asteroid project.
