chapters.title: Chapter 684: The Dragon Necromancer’s Revenge (2)
paragraphs: Crack.
Boom.

"Impossible... I don’t believe you are stronger than me... That is impossible," Tiger King Tyron said, rising from the ground with a broken jaw, bleeding nose, dislocated shoulder, and—well—his face was just broken beyond repair.

Yi Lai stood a few meters away from him, looking perfectly fine. She had no blood on her—the blood on her wasn’t hers—but the blood of her opponent, now coating her fist, showing how powerful she had become.
"I don’t believe that in just under two years you have surpassed my thousands of years of effort... I don’t believe it."
Yi Lai chuckled. "Then become a believer, because this is happening."

She moved, and before King Tyron could sense her movement, she was already on him with her fist planted on his jaw. The force behind the punch pushed him back several meters, but Yi Lai was on him the next second.
The battle hadn’t been going on for long, but she had already destroyed King Tyron’s face and arms without much struggle.
Yi Lai was not stronger than King Tyron’s strength-wise, but when it came to speed, she was three, perhaps four times faster.
So she may not be strong, but she made up for the gap in strength with her speed, and since you can only punch what you can keep up with, King Tyron wasn’t having a good day, to say the least.
Yi Lai was having a field day with him, and that alone was showing in the number of bones she was breaking.
Meanwhile, Veera and her undead swordsmen were almost done with the battle. Nethar, Yi Lai’s undead dragon, was enough to handle the weaker tigers. So Veera’s joining was overkill.

But thanks to her joining, things ended much faster. When the battle came to an end, she turned and looked in Yi Lai’s direction. "Well, she is really taking her time to get her pain out... good for her."
Veera smiled and then turned toward Nether, who was just standing there watching Yi Lai trash the Tiger King.
Boom.

Yi Lai sucker-punched the Tiger King, sending him flying back. His body was broken beyond repair, and judging by how long it took him to stand up, this time, she became a believer and knew he was done for.
However, when he saw that all his ambush of Tigers had been killed, his aura took on a deeper and darker turn, transforming into his 25-meter tall True Beast form.
It had red fur, with some metallic coatings around its legs and head. These partially covered his body, serving both as defense and decoration, showcasing his elegance.
But Yi Lai didn’t care about that. Her mission was to make the bastard suffer before dying, and so far, she had succeeded in the suffering part. Now only the dying part remained...

The moment King Tyron became a tiger, he lunged at Yi Lai, who didn’t even flinch. That was because she knew the Tiger couldn’t keep up with her in the first place. So the moment the tiger came closer to her with his claw, she moved and drove her fist into the tiger’s neck.
The punch was powerful enough to send him flying back. She moved and appeared in front of the Tiger, which towered over her.

However, disregarding the tiger’s imposing height, she formed a bolt of dark lightning and struck it. It exploded upon contact, forcing the Tiger to let out a powerful roar and stagger, falling a few seconds later.
Yi Lai smirked and then summoned her sword. She unleashed two powerful sword arcs, striking the thick, incredibly hard, metallic-coated legs of the tiger, rendering him immobile.
When she got closer, she rose slowly into the air and stared down at the tiger. "Not so tough now, are you?"
The tiger roared furiously, trying to muster the courage to stand... but it just wasn’t possible. However, that didn’t stop him from sending a blast of red energy, which Yi Lai evaded effortlessly.
"All the humiliations I suffered at your hands a hundred years ago... I finally got my revenge. So you should die knowing your bad decisions were the cause of your doom.
I will sleep now, knowing you and your kind are no more..."

She raised her sword, and then, up in the air, a bigger version of her sword manifested. It was taller, thinner, and sharper. However, the moment she gestured downward, the sword moved and drew a hole through King Tyron’s head—ending his damn existence for good.
Yi Lai exhaled and then landed softly on the ground.
"Happy now?" Veera appeared the next second and stood beside Yi Lai.
"I guess I am... the years of hatred have been vented... The only ones left are the Oracles and the Hand. But I will deal with the Oracles now and the Hand later."
Veera just shook her head and smiled...
"In any case, I won’t be taking this beast... He was just too weak to be a worthy undead. Although I doubt I will gain much from the ones we will face soon... But at least they will be humanoids."
Yi Lai nodded.

If she had the means to raise undead, she most certainly wouldn’t have raised the tiger as her undead either. It wouldn’t be because she hated him—well, that is part of it—but she most certainly wouldn’t take such a weakling as her undead soldier.
Veera had the means to make the Tiger King stronger over time, but she already had enough weaklings she was nurturing with far superior items than the body of King Tyron.
"Then why don’t we leave for the main mission... I doubt there is something else here for us," Veera said, and Yi Lai nodded.
"Let’s go." She touched Veera’s shoulder, and the next second, they vanished. Nethar had already disappeared into Yi Lai’s body, so they left and appeared somewhere in Vastport City.
The moment they appeared, Yi Lai took out a device and channeled her energy into it... A few seconds later, a red orb appeared from it and started flying away.
"Let’s go." With that, they started moving after the red orb.

chapters.title: Chapter 685: The Dragon Necromancer’s Revenge (3) [Bonus]
paragraphs: The Oracle headquarters was considered one of the most secure locations in the world. It was located in a pocket dimension, and unless you had the mark of the Oracles, you wouldn’t be able to find the gates, let alone enter.
Many tried over the years, and they all failed miserably.
Basically, the Oracle headquarters was a fortress that couldn’t be breached.
However, it was breached today, and the one who did it was the last person they wanted to see.
They didn’t know that the hunter they had sent into the Dead Region had infiltrated their domain. They never saw that far into their reckless planning and now, it came back to bite them in the ass.
But of course, they didn’t recognize her, and while it would have been polite to talk things out, they knew she hadn’t come for conversation.
After all, she breached their safe space and was exuding potent killing intent. There was no need to think otherwise.
So they attacked, employing a range of soul-attacking skills. However, all their attacks were rendered useless, considering Yi Lai held her sword.
Her sword was the same as her scepter. Since it could render most soul attacks useless, the Oracles, who weren’t known for their combat powers, found themselves in a precarious situation.
None of their soul attacks were working.
However, Yi Lai showed no mercy at all.
She came to kill, and that was all her mind was set on. Despite their painful cries, she didn’t stop her massacre. Nothing would compel her to stop her revenge on those who had wronged her.
There weren’t only humans there; there were elves, demons, and even beastkin. The Oracles were a big organization recognized in Sonox, so it was only natural to have members from other races.
But even so, Yi Lai wasn’t holding back her attacks. She knew soon the big bosses would appear, and while she couldn’t wait to get them under her sword, she couldn’t let these weaklings leave either.
The moment she breached the headquarters, all Oracles in the world sensed the danger, so they came to defend—only to be met with failure at every second.
Veera was having a field day with them, while Nethar was also making sure they died engulfed in flames. The beautiful space the three found themselves in now was littered with flames and blood.

"Everyone, use your life-saving treasures and leave now." When more started dying, the leader of the Oracles, a strikingly beautiful woman, appeared in the air. Behind her were sixteen ladies, each exuding a powerful presence.
The Oracles who heard their leader’s voice immediately activated their teleportation devices tethered to the outside. However, to their shock, their teleportation devices stopped working.
"WHAT?"
Everyone’s face turned grim.
This wasn’t what they expected.

As Oracles, they knew that at some point they would be required to make a quick exit, so the moment a new member was welcomed into their fold, they were given these specially designed teleporters to aid them in a swift escape.

These devices had helped them greatly. As people who practiced extracting the life force from men they slept with, it wasn’t too hard to realize they needed something like a quick and portable teleporter. In case anything bad happened, they always had a way out.
But not today... Their precious life-saving treasures aren’t working.
This was because all exits were blocked. Yi Lai wanted to kill everyone, so obviously she came prepared, primarily since she was associated with someone like Kent.

"Who are you?" the leader of the Oracles—or as they called her, Lady Oracle—asked in a grim tone. They had heard of the Hunter and knew her, but the one they knew was just a puppet controlled by her, meaning this was their first time seeing her in person.

However, even if they had seen her before, Yi Lai had come a long way from how she looked a couple of years ago... and to her, it had already been fifty years. Therefore, many changes were likely to have occurred.
But poor Oracles, they had no idea their plan to get rid of two nuisances had now become a headache for them.
They wanted Kent and Hunter gone...but it now turns out they made a grave mistake picking an enemy they never knew would one day come seeking revenge.

Yi Lai stopped her attack and looked at the Oracles; then a smirk formed on her lips. "Well, I can’t blame you if you don’t know who I am... after all, even the people who saved me don’t know what I look like... Only one person ever did."

Her mind flashed back to Kent—he was the only person who had managed to bring out her true self. For years, nobody knew what she looked like, so the day Kent found her true body was the day she developed some respect for him.
"Two years ago, you sent that lady to kill me by sending me to the Dead Region... Does that ring a bell?"
"THE HUNTER!"
Everyone’s face turned grim when they heard her.
"I go by a different name now... but yes... the same hunter you tried to kill despite me not doing anything to you." Yi Lai smiled.
Around her, Veera and her undead swordsmen and a few assassins were doing the most, killing as if it were the most natural thing to do.
"Isn’t it ironic... I’ve done nothing to you... But due to hunger for power and perhaps a sense of fulfillment, you chose to hunt me down and kill me." She chuckled.

"It turns out that decision you made was the turning point for me... and the beginning of your doom." Her smile turned funny. "Don’t worry, I don’t plan on killing everyone—my master said I should keep one of you to deliver his message."
"And who is your master?" Lady Oracle asked.
Yi Lai smiled. "Kent Madson... also, it turns out he isn’t that evil... he is actually a good person... But I guess that is now too late for perverts portraying themselves as Oracles."
Her laughter filled the space, carrying a touch of mockery that made the Oracles seethe with anger, yet also shudder with fear.
"Surround her... if we can’t leave, then we might as well take her with us." That was their last desperate struggle—a moment when they thought they had everything figured out.

One filled with the idea that they could wiggle their way out of the claws of death. However, Yi Lai planned to shatter those dreams from the start... She wanted them to die knowing there was nothing they could do.
"Nethar, do the things."
The redheaded undead dragon smiled when he heard his master’s command.
The Oracles began gathering their strength and determination to fight back when a sudden roar filled the space, shattering all their hope...
A red dragon spread its wings, and fire started filling the space...

chapters.title: Chapter 686: Revenged [Bonus]
paragraphs: The battle after Nethar took his dragon form was quick and decisive. Yi Lai never even had to do anything. She just stood there, keeping her eyes on everything, watching them scream.
It was a chaotic and devastating display that left them all screaming before they succumbed to death. In the end, only Lady Oracle remained alive.
Yi Lai did say she would keep one of them, and so she saved the strongest.

She wasn’t stupid; she knew that if anyone had the means to deliver her master’s message to the Hand, it would be the leader of one of the world’s most dangerous organizations—not anymore—but she held some authority.
To some extent, she does again, and so she knew Lady Oracle would be able to deliver Kent’s message.
"Nicely done, Nethar," Yi Lai praised her only undead and then turned to the only surviving member of the Oracles... their leader.
"I know you’re probably angry... I mean, when the previous leader was ascending, she probably told you one day you would be joining her and continuing your perverted legacy in the high worlds.
Guess what? She was wrong, and you are proof of that. You watched your entire organization get slaughtered. That means you are a failure...and there is no denying that.
However, don’t worry, I don’t have much energy to waste on trash-talking you, so let’s get down to business, shall we?"
Veera shook her head, hearing Yi Lai’s sassy words. ’It turns out getting her revenge made her more relatable and a little sassy...’

She turned and looked at the Lady Oracle, smirking. "Are you sure we shouldn’t kill her and wake her up? That would be much more convenient," Veera asked, causing the poor Oracle to shudder in her bones.
Yi Lai thought about what Veera said for a second, then she smiled. "She is not destined to die today... But the next time we meet, she will die for sure."
Veera just smirked and turned away. Since nobody else was dying anymore, she lost interest in the rest...
"Listen carefully. The only reason you are alive now is because my master wants someone to deliver his message to the Hand. Naturally, that will be your job now...

Go to them and be sure not to leave out even a single word. Tell them, and I quote, ’You have three years to open the Gate of the Apocalypse. Failure to meet this deadline will result in severe consequences. Kent Madson sent his greetings, by the way."
Yi Lai walked closer and stared her daggers in the eye. "No word less, not a word more. And if you want, you can come for revenge... Killing you won’t be too hard... Lady Oracle."
With that, Yi Lai left with her people. What she had come there to do was over, and now she had to get back to her master.
Since they were connected to the tower, they merely vanished, leaving the Oracle Lady to ponder what to do next.
But pondering on what to do was the least of her worries now. What she had spent years working to build and maintain was destroyed within a couple of minutes.
That was both shocking, devastating, and disgraceful.
She claimed to hold the power that could cause kingdoms to respect her. She claimed she had the power to be known as one of the strongest organizations in the world of Sonox.
She held the power to make sects bow to her. She held the power to make powerhouses shudder before they even thought of going against her.
The kind of power she held was supreme in this world and perhaps every other medium world out there. However, it took only three people to destroy everything she had built.
The shocking part was that these three people were able to destroy everything she had built and developed over several years without even breaking a sweat.
Some things she thought could never be destroyed. Something she thought could rival other powerful organizations was destroyed, leaving her in a state of shock.
Devastating because, while she could fathom losing to the Hand, who are also known as the strongest in the world, she never expected her ending to come crashing down like this.
Then came the disgraceful part, where at the moment she had been reduced to an errand girl. It felt too disgraceful.
She could accept the shock and devastation, but accepting the disgrace was eating at her pride.
This led her to break down. However, the deed had already been done, and after a while, she left. She wanted to deliver the message and then plot her revenge.
The artificial island where the Hand’s headquarters were located wasn’t accessible to just anyone. It is a place much like the Oracle’s headquarters, accessible only to members of the Hand.
However, unlike the Oracles, not everyone in the organization can just walk in. Only the top-ranking members of the Hand get to come there or even know it exists.
Today, someone outside the Hand entered, and this person was the last person the Hand wanted to see.
Instead of attacking her, they chose to hear what she had to say, as she claimed to have a message for them.
Now she was having her audience with the Hand, who were accompanied by the Seven Fangs of the Hand.

"Well, Lady Oracle, what brought you to the Hand?" the Hand asked, looking as beautiful as ever. Though she is in charge of one of the most notorious organizations in the world, one can’t deny her good looks.
Lady Oracle doesn’t pale in the beauty department. However, the Hand is just too gorgeous by all standards.

"Kent Madson has a message for you. And before you ask if I am affiliated with him... the answer is no. However, I just lost my entire organization when he sent his associate, whom I am sure you all know all too well—the Hunter.

He said I should tell you, and I quote, ’You have three years to open the Gate of the Apocalypse. Failure to meet this deadline will result in severe consequences. Kent Madson sent his greetings, by the way."
The moment she was done, she stood up and started walking away. But before she left, she turned and gave them one last good look.
"If you have what it takes to kill him, then do it fast... However, leave the Hunter for me... she will die at my hand."
With that, she left, leaving the Hand and her seven generals in a state of shock and anger...

Instead of attacking her, they chose to hear what she had to say, as she claimed to have a message for them.
Now she was having her audience with the Hand, who were accompanied by the Seven Fangs of the Hand.
"Well, Lady Oracle, what brought you to the Hand?" the Hand asked, looking as beautiful as ever.
Though she is in charge of one of the most notorious organizations in the world, one can’t deny her good looks.
Lady Oracle doesn’t pale in the beauty department.
However, the Hand is just too gorgeous by all standards.
"Kent Madson has a message for you.
And before you ask if I am affiliated with him... the answer is no.
However, I just lost my entire organization when he sent his associate, whom I am sure you all know all too well—the Hunter.
He said I should tell you, and I quote, ’You have three years to open the Gate of the Apocalypse.
Failure to meet this deadline will result in severe consequences.
Kent Madson sent his greetings, by the way."
The moment she was done, she stood up and started walking away.
But before she left, she turned and gave them one last good look.
"If you have what it takes to kill him, then do it fast...
However, leave the Hunter for me... she will die at my hand."
With that, she left, leaving the Hand and her seven generals in a state of shock and anger...

chapters.title: Chapter 687: The Hand is Angry
paragraphs: First of all, the Hand didn’t even know what to think.
Yes... They are the strongest underworld organization in the world. Yes... Nobody dares challenge them. And yes, they have the same authority as kings and queens.
Naturally, they have what it takes to make a kingdom bleed. So such an organization isn’t one to take for granted.
Yet, Kent Madson did, and the implications are something nobody can even fathom. The daring nature of Kent Madson has finally made the Hand angry—and they are, in fact, very angry.
First, not only did Kent know their main goals and plans for the world, but he also knew what had to be done and what the end product would be.

If they didn’t know better, they would say he was a part of them, that he was there when they discussed their plans to bring about the end of the world. They would say he had spies in their organization, and for that, they had to do a purge.
They had to identify the spy(s) in their organization and handle them effectively. That was the only logical explanation for the fact that Kent knew their biggest secret.
However, crazy as it may sound, they knew they had no spies in their organization. But even if they did, it wasn’t as if the spies knew of something this sensitive and managed to tell an outsider.
The moment they utter a word of it to an outsider, they would know, and the person who betrays them will die without fail. They wouldn’t even be done divulging the secret before death kicks in.
And even if the person somehow manages to say something, aside from the eight of them in the room, nobody else knew of the doomsday plan they were cooking up.
So they knew Kent came about this information in some other way.
But just how?
Such information is not easily obtainable. This means that Kent is indeed dangerous, and that alone left the people shocked and scared.

Yes... They are scared, and it isn’t because they just heard the Oracles are no more. They are scared because, for the first time since the Hand was formed, someone actually had the courage to command them.
Kent commanded them to do what they wanted to do in the first place. That means he isn’t afraid of them, and he isn’t afraid to show it.
This also means the fear around them—the one that is even making the Dragons become wary of them—isn’t something Kent cares about.
That was just too arrogant, and as such, they wanted blood.

"Deploy everyone... activate all sleeper warriors and contact all our allies... and if that is not enough, your seven should go personally and ensure his head is on a silver platter the next time I see your faces," the Hand shouted, showing how angry she had become.
Not that the seven people around her weren’t also angry—they each felt like ripping Kent into shreds.
"We will get it done, my lady." With that, they left, leaving the Hand to herself.
The Seven Fangs of the Hand had already shown interest in hunting Kent down, so this was a golden opportunity for them to get just what they wanted.
After the Hand left the meeting hall, she entered an underground chamber that led deeper into the ground. After moving for a while, she came to a stop in front of a small door.
She sighed deeply, then opened it and entered. The room was painted black—every part of it painted black. However, aside from the black paint, a black mirror was also hanging on the facing wall.
She took a moment, then spoke to the mirror.
"We have a problem." For a moment, nothing happened; however, after a few seconds, the mirror shimmered, and then a face appeared on it.

It was that of a lady, a very beautiful lady with two crystal-red horns on her forehead. She wasn’t a dragon, but judging by the horns and the fact that she had much longer ears, it was clear she might be a hybrid of a dragon and an elf.
"Speak, my child," the voice said in a tone that was both soothing and authoritative.

"There is a human threat to our plans. I am afraid that if he is not taken care of, we might face complications... I have already activated all the forces we have... but I want him gone, so I want your assistance."

There was a pause, then the lady in the mirror smiled. "It has been 27,000 years, Amix. You never once asked for my assistance, unlike your sisters. So if you are asking now, it must mean you are facing a rather severe problem.
Come on, tell me more about this human while we still have time... the laws are closing in."
Amix, the leader of the Hand sign, then began to speak. "His name is Kent Madson... he came out of nowhere and started causing trouble for everyone.

I used some of my assets to handle him, but he took care of them, and, well, some betrayed me... not that I expected anything less from such an asset... but he is good at hiding, and so far, I can’t pinpoint where he is.
But he is resourceful. So I doubt he can be easily taken care of without your help."
"He doesn’t sound like an enemy to me. Why don’t you make him your ally?" the lady in the mirror suggested.
"That is not possible. And I have no place to make him an ally... However, you should know he owns a Divine Atomic Body and he knew about our plans to open the Gate of the Apocalypse..."
"What?" The lady in the mirror frowned. "He must be eliminated... and fast." The lady in the mirror paused for a few minutes, then spoke again.
"The Ancient race has stirred. I authorize you to use the method and unleash them after this, Kent Madson. Give them the same deal... if they help, they will get as much blood from the Wynthralls.
With them, this Kent Madson will fall regardless of his resourcefulness."
The face vanished from the mirror, but her voice echoed in Amix’s head. "Do not fail, Amix. Lord Immortal won’t be happy if you fail."

chapters.title: Chapter 688: Entering The Planet Killer Dungeon
paragraphs: "So, how was it?" Kent asked Yi Lai the moment she got back to the Tower with her team. In the end, the battle was quick and decisive, and the plans she had for Veera were also scrapped.
The bodies they dropped were just too weak to be worthy of being called undead under someone like Veera’s command. It just doesn’t sound or feel right.
However, there is a silver lining to it, and that is the souls she harvested. Those would soon enable her to summon a more powerful undead.
"It went well...I managed to get my affairs in order." Yi Lai smiled, "I can now get down to business."
Kent nodded and smiled..."Good to hear that Yi Lai, because as it turns out, I have a bigger mission for you all...and I am afraid, this will take years to complete."
The moment the words left Kent’s mouth, Kaizo moved closer with a broad smile playing on his face. Hearing that there was a mission made him feel like a child waiting for Santa at the mall.
’I guess that is how he is...always happy for the next battle,’ Kent mused and then turned to face everyone.
"This new mission will take some time to complete...but that is just the simplest aspect of it. When it comes down to how hard it will be, let me tell you, things will be much more chaotic.

The place you will be fighting is a dungeon, but unlike the ones you have entered and cleared, this one is different. It is unique if you may, and while the highest level you ever went was 17, this one contains 37 levels.

It also has more harrowing dangers than the previous ones. I am yet to understand the extent to which this dungeon goes, but I know that the weakest being your will fight in the dungeon is at the peak of the core formations stage.

This means the chances of facing a spirit Ascension or a spirit king at just the first level are already this harrowing. However, I have hopes that you will manage somehow," Kent smiles, watching the faces of his legion.

They all seem pumped for battle...but they had no idea the kind of danger they would find themselves in. But they aren’t normal beings, and per the quest message, many rewards are waiting for not only him, but his wives and legion.
So he knew that after the suffering, they would reap the benefits too.
"I have a question, master..." Sylara spoke, and Kent gestured for her to talk.
"Are the beasts or creatures inside the dungeon real. I know the ones inside the other dungeons are made of spiritual Qi, so would these too be the same?"

Sylara is asking not because she wants the well-being of her friends and teammates...she was asking for herself. The blood from the beasts that were killed in the dungeons she had explored was not genuine.
Drinking it makes her stomach ick, so she wanted to know more about the nature of the next dungeon, and if it is to her satisfaction, she wouldn’t hesitate to go all out.

Also, aside from her quest to fill her stomach with real blood, she is also concerned about her bloodline. To date, she still hadn’t told anyone what her bloodline is...but she was bound to do so soon.

"Everything inside the dungeon is real, and unlike the dungeons you had already cleared, this one has no respawn feature. It means there is only one life for you all..." Kent paused and looked at Kaizo and his other undead...
"Some of you at least." His undead can’t die, regardless of how many times they’ve been killed. The only downside is that he will need twice as many resources used in creating them to revive them.
But they can’t die...
"I will clear the first level with you all before I leave. After the first floor, I will get a good read on things. After which you and my ladies can proceed from there." They all nodded.
"Alright, get your affairs in order...those of you who have friends in the cities, you can go tell them you will be away for a while."

They nodded and left. Kent knew they could easily come into the tower to relax, but that would be for a few days...and since time passes differently on the outside, a week for them inside the dungeon is several months inside the tower, so they better say their goodbyes for now.

His ladies are already doing that, and he did the same with Li Hua and the Cosmic Lolis. Of course, he promised to come see them regularly, even when he is away on the other continents, since he still has a lot to do, aside from finding ways to reach the Pill Princess.
For now, he knew things would become much more chaotic the moment he left the tower. The Hand had already made their move, and he would have to do his too.
He wanted to start with the Primal Bone Tempering Art before going out there, but now it seems he had to get things done with his current strength.
’Who am I kidding, with what my bloodline can do...these people won’t know what hit them.’ Just like that, Kent knew he would soon be having a wild ride.
But first, he needed to take his wives and the legion to the dungeon. He had already said his goodbyes to Elaine’s parents and Velyra’s father, so he will be off and away for a while.
Thankfully, he knew exactly where to go and how to get there.
It took a couple of hours, but everyone managed to get their affairs in order. Kent brought them all to the mountain garden for one final info...

"There will be beings far stronger than you in the dungeon. However, while that should discourage you...Use it as the catalyst to temper your combat skills and learn how to handle those several realms above you.
Because trust me, as long as you all are connected to me, the dangers that will come will be much more dangerous than you think."
They smiled.
"That said, I expect you all to make great strides before we ascend to a high world." The nodded, and Kent activated the dungeon transporter, disappearing from sight

chapters.title: Chapter 689: First Floor - Four Floating Islands [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent appeared inside the dungeon, landing on soft ground...
"A river bank, huh?" Kent studied his surroundings and saw he was standing on the bank of a river. Looking ahead, he could see a vast body of water extending several kilometers.
The water was greyish, and judging by the vapor rising from it, Kent knew it wouldn’t be easy to swim in. The water looked like the kind that would suck the spiritual qi out of anything that entered.
"I am definitely not getting into this water."

After making up his mind, Kent turned to the message he had received the moment he entered the dungeon. He saw nothing aside from the water, so he had to gain some insight somehow, and it seemed the tower had prepared one for him.
⟦Welcome to the Planet Killer Dungeon. Your 12-year duration has begun, and the dungeon must be cleared before the duration is over⟧
⟦Name: Planet Killer Dungeon⟧
⟦Floor Name: Four Floating Islands (1st)⟧
⟦Power Level: Core Formation - Spirit Ascension (peak)⟧
⟦Description:
The first floor of the Planet Killer Dungeon is home to the Metal Spiders. They are poisonous and deadly. A single scratch is enough to paralyze their foe.
Additionally, falling into the water can cause some unwanted pain, so avoid doing that as well.⟧
Objective:

↠ You and your team must clear all four dungeons at the same time. All battles shouldn’t end ten minutes apart. There are 400 Metal Spiders on every island, and the floor boss of this floor is located on the Middle Island.
↠ Aside from the Core formation stage, each island has between level 4 and 7 Spirit Ascension stage, six Metal Spiders. However, the boss is at the Peak Spirit Ascension stage.
⟦Rewards⟧
↠ 1 Million Tower Points
↠ 1,000,500,000 Soul Essence
↠ Unknown Poison Recipe
↠ Unknown Bone Tempering Elixir
↠ Map of the Planet Killer Dungeon

⟦Note: All drops will be stored inside the Tower storage. Additionally, it is advisable to thoroughly explore the floors using the dungeon map, as there are hidden items that can only be discovered with detailed examination.⟧

"I guess things aren’t that hard in the first trial. And oh, as for the poison, we have the wicked Poison Witch with us, so that is a bonus then." Kent smiled and then walked away from the riverbank, summoned his legion, and his wives.
The moment they appeared, their expressions turned dazed. Looking at the water stretching far and wide, they couldn’t help but wonder about many things in their heads.
However, Kent immediately cleared their doubts by snapping his fingers. The moment he did that, four floating islands came into view.
Three islands formed a triangle around the fourth island, which Kent knew was the location of the boss. The objective clearly said the boss was on the middle island.
Vexthra moved into Kent’s arm. "So what is the plan?" she asked. She is the leader who will handle the mission Kent had given them.

Kent wanted to take her on his mission to the other continents, but she said no. Vexthra wasn’t the kind of person who would pick a few moments of respite outside if that meant taking more of her man’s time.

She explained that Kent needed to reach the High Worlds faster because that is where he would gain more, so tagging along now would only bring him more problems that he would have to waste time on, instead of focusing on his mission.
But aside from that, she also wanted to stay close to her sisters, since although she couldn’t fight with them, she could heal them when things went bad.
Thanks to the Tower connecting them together, healing them to some extent wouldn’t call the wrath of the heavenly laws upon her.
Then, one last thing: she wanted to experience what it was like to explore a Unique Dungeon. It turns out gods also have quirks, and one of hers was exploring dungeons.
Kent just smiled and nodded in response to her words. But he planned to summon her when he got to the other continents and perhaps spend a few hours with her every now and then.

Kent kissed her hair and then answered her question. "This is the Four Floating Islands floor, and as its name suggests, there are indeed four floating islands, each housing a type of beast known as the Metal Spiders.
There are 400 such spiders on each island, and they range from the Core Formation stage to the Spirit Ascension. We have to clear all four islands, and then we can explore them.
And like I said back in the tower, there will be rewards for all of us at the end of every mission, so be sure not to lose the storage rings I gave you."
They nodded, and Kent turned toward the islands. "We need to form four teams... Since there are just 400 spiders on each island, we might as well do well to get them all quickly."
Kent turned back to his team and then started sharing the teams. It took a few minutes, but he managed to get the four teams ready.
His team would handle the middle island, as that is where the floor boss is located. However, Kent didn’t even want to fight... He wanted to see his ladies and legions in action.
"So, how do we get to the islands? Do we fly?" Krex asked, already looking forward to fighting the peak Core Formation spiders.
Since he was the weakest on the team, he was eager to prove himself to his older siblings. He wanted to see if he had what it takes to be on the team.
"I can just send you all to your islands with a flick of my hand. However, you can also fly there, which I know wouldn’t be as simple as you think, so why don’t I send you there?"
They all nodded.
"Then, happy hunting," Kent waved his hand, and all four teams vanished. The only ones left were he and Vexthra.
"After I am gone, you will have some form of control over the Tower, which will allow you to know the nature of the dungeon and what has to be done to clear every floor you find yourself on.
I will also make it so they all can appraise their rewards and know how to use them," Kent said, and Vexthra nodded.
With that, they also vanished and appeared on the middle floating island...

"I guess things aren’t that hard in the first trial.
And oh, as for the poison, we have the wicked Poison Witch with us, so that is a bonus then." Kent smiled and then walked away from the riverbank, summoned his legion, and his wives.
The moment they appeared, their expressions turned dazed.
Looking at the water stretching far and wide, they couldn’t help but wonder about many things in their heads.
However, Kent immediately cleared their doubts by snapping his fingers.
The moment he did that, four floating islands came into view.
Three islands formed a triangle around the fourth island, which Kent knew was the location of the boss.
The objective clearly said the boss was on the middle island.
Vexthra moved into Kent’s arm.
"So what is the plan?" she asked.
She is the leader who will handle the mission Kent had given them.
Kent wanted to take her on his mission to the other continents, but she said no.
Vexthra wasn’t the kind of person who would pick a few moments of respite outside if that meant taking more of her man’s time.

She explained that Kent needed to reach the High Worlds faster because that is where he would gain more, so tagging along now would only bring him more problems that he would have to waste time on, instead of focusing on his mission.
But aside from that, she also wanted to stay close to her sisters, since although she couldn’t fight with them, she could heal them when things went bad.
Thanks to the Tower connecting them together, healing them to some extent wouldn’t call the wrath of the heavenly laws upon her.
Then, one last thing: she wanted to experience what it was like to explore a Unique Dungeon.
It turns out gods also have quirks, and one of hers was exploring dungeons.
Kent just smiled and nodded in response to her words.
But he planned to summon her when he got to the other continents and perhaps spend a few hours with her every now and then.
Kent kissed her hair and then answered her question.
"This is the Four Floating Islands floor, and as its name suggests, there are indeed four floating islands, each housing a type of beast known as the Metal Spiders.
There are 400 such spiders on each island, and they range from the Core Formation stage to the Spirit Ascension.
We have to clear all four islands, and then we can explore them.
And like I said back in the tower, there will be rewards for all of us at the end of every mission, so be sure not to lose the storage rings I gave you."
They nodded, and Kent turned toward the islands.
"We need to form four teams...
Since there are just 400 spiders on each island, we might as well do well to get them all quickly."
Kent turned back to his team and then started sharing the teams.
It took a few minutes, but he managed to get the four teams ready.
His team would handle the middle island, as that is where the floor boss is located.
However, Kent didn’t even want to fight...
He wanted to see his ladies and legions in action.
"So, how do we get to the islands?
Do we fly?" Krex asked, already looking forward to fighting the peak Core Formation spiders.
Since he was the weakest on the team, he was eager to prove himself to his older siblings.
He wanted to see if he had what it takes to be on the team.
"I can just send you all to your islands with a flick of my hand.
However, you can also fly there, which I know wouldn’t be as simple as you think, so why don’t I send you there?"
They all nodded.
"Then, happy hunting," Kent waved his hand, and all four teams vanished.
The only ones left were he and Vexthra.
"After I am gone, you will have some form of control over the Tower, which will allow you to know the nature of the dungeon and what has to be done to clear every floor you find yourself on.
I will also make it so they all can appraise their rewards and know how to use them," Kent said, and Vexthra nodded.
With that, they also vanished and appeared on the middle floating island...

chapters.title: Chapter 690: First Floor Battle (1) [Bonus]
paragraphs: The surface of the floating island, where Kent and Vexthra landed, was a dense forest alive with vibrant shades of green.

Towering ancient trees stretched high into the misty sky, their thick trunks wrapped in twisting vines and moss. Their broad canopies formed a natural ceiling, filtering sunlight into soft, dappled patterns on the forest floor below.
Among the giants were smaller trees and shrubs, bursting with colorful blossoms and thick foliage.
The air was rich with the scent of earth and blooming flora, mingled with a faint, metallic tang—perhaps a warning of the dangerous Metal Spiders lurking within.
Underneath, the forest floor was carpeted with a mix of soft moss, fallen leaves, and tangled roots that twisted and curled like serpents.
Occasional shafts of light pierced the canopy, spotlighting patches of vibrant mushrooms and luminescent plants that glowed faintly in the dim light.
However, while this place looked breathtaking, the danger hiding within wasn’t something to be taken lightly.

The moment Kent and Vexthra arrived, they were attacked by a 12-meter-long spider with piercing legs. Its body was compact and covered in segmented metallic plates that shimmered with a dark iron-blue hue.
Its limbs were slender but razor-sharp, ending in claw-like pincers that could pierce armor. Looking at its misty body, it wasn’t hard to tell that it was exuding toxic poison.

One slender metallic leg came close to piercing Vexthra’s chest. However, Kent was quick. He took Vexthra’s hand and twirled her like a princess while his sword appeared in his other hand, taking a fast swing.
Dozens of sword lights flashed out, cutting the spider into pieces. It was a precise strike that left the spider dying in chunks.
Vexthra fell into Kent’s arms as he slowly rose into the air with the goddess in his arms. They moved forward to observe the battle happening on the battlefield.
The team fighting on the middle island consisted of Unity, Camilla, Alina, Ingrid, Kaizo, Skoggr, Valtor, Irina, and Krex.
Kent knew the battle on the middle island would be the hardest, as it would involve multiple Spirit Ascension stage spiders and the Floor Boss.
However, he knew his team had what it took to get it done. They were some of the finest warriors he had seen, and so he knew they had what it took to complete the job.
However, while that one is obvious, the process is a little tedious. The spiders have legs so long that someone like Vari, who uses daggers, finds it taxing to get close and deal deadly blows.
So instead of using her daggers to kill up close, she threw them at the spiders, each finding its mark.

However, while the daggers she threw eventually came back to her, her killing speed has decreased considerably. That is the only disadvantage she has. The rest is countered thanks to her reaction speed. It is unprecedented.
On the middle island, Unity was firing arrows so lethal that a single shot was all it took to kill multiple targets. It felt so dreamy watching her impeccable display of archery skills.

It was like she was born with the bow. Naturally, one of her Primordial spirits uses the bow, and since she has no true name yet, her Primordial spirits are still at Tier 18, making them a force to reckon with.
Inside her soul sea, the Feisty Primordial spirit sat in a lotus posture, a Tier 14 spell diagram opened in front of her, facing her like a wall.
Outside, the same spell circle appeared around Unity’s arm as she fired one arrow after another. This display made the Feisty Primordial spirit grin from ear to ear.

The Blossom Primordial spirit, who was much more elegant, sat behind a canvas, painting an arrow. Watching her sister, Feisty, giggle whenever Unity landed a triple kill, she just didn’t have the words to describe her.
"What are you looking at?" Feisty asked, grinning at Blossom. The look in her eyes said it all; she was having the time of her life.
Blossom shook her head. "Nothing..." In the end, Blossom decided to focus on her painting. Feisty smirked and then chose to disturb Blossom.
"Are you done yet with the arrow? We need it to kill the Floor Boss... so better hurry."

"Don’t rush me, okay. Unlike you, who likes making all the wrong choices, I actually think before doing something... anything." Blossom didn’t even turn to look at her. She was more focused on her painting.
Feisty, hearing Blossom’s words, smirked. "You are forgetting we are the same. It’s just that I am more interesting and you are just gloomy."
"Whatever, I want to kill the Floor Boss before the brute does."
The brute she was talking about was Kaizo, who was like the angel of death on the battlefield. From ripping the legs off spiders to punching holes in their bodies, Kaizo was obliterating them all.
"Hahaha... This is fun," Kaizo shouted as he jumped several meters high and landed a powerful punch on a spider as he descended, shaking the entire floating island.
"Hey Kaizo, some of us can’t swim, so better not send the island into the water," Skoggr, the Orc Chieftain, said, making Kent grin.
"Don’t worry, I used just 30% of my power... I’m sure that won’t sink the floating island."
Skoggr and the others just smirked. Kaizo didn’t lie, but the fact that 30% of his strength shook the entire island was a little concerning.
Camilla was making her way along the edge of the island when she sensed a powerful presence coming from a couple of kilometers away.
She immediately recognized the aura to be that of a Spirit Ascension stage beast.
"Uhm, people, I think the Floor Boss is coming," Camilla shouted, drawing everyone’s attention. They turned to her direction, but before they could move, Kent’s voice reached their ears.
"That is not the Floor Boss. Though this is not a normal dungeon, the Floor Boss will appear when all the small fries have been dealt with."
Hearing his words, they all nodded and went back to killing more spiders. Camilla smiled, knowing the Spirit Ascension spider was hers to handle.
"Time to get to work, Dawn." The spear in her hand vibrated, giving off a brilliant light.
"About damn time," the spear spoke, bringing a smile to Camilla’s face. The next second, a giant spider with an even more metallic body and legs appeared, towering over Camilla.

chapters.title: Chapter 691: First Floor Battle (2) [Bonus]
paragraphs: The Ascension stage Metal Spider truly lives up to its name.

Unlike the metal spiders at the Core Formation stage, which have 12-meter-long legs, this one’s legs stretch an imposing 20 meters, and its body is colossal, with thick, armored plates gleaming with an eerie metallic sheen that seems almost impervious to ordinary weapons.
Just looking at it conveys the message that it isn’t an easy target to cut.
Its segmented exoskeleton pulses faintly with toxic, mist-like energy, veins of glowing blue light tracing intricate patterns across its surface.
It appears to have been decorated with ancient runes, when, in fact, the patterns are merely there to make it even more imposing.
Camilla trails her eyes across its limbs, long and slender yet bristling with sharp barbs, ending in pincers capable of crushing metals.
"That is one hideous yet terrifying spider," Camilla smirked, watching the spider emerge from the thickness of the forest.
It has multiple eyes glinting like shards of obsidian. As it moves, the ground trembles beneath its weight, sending vibrations through the floating island’s surface.
Thick, steam-like mist coils off its body, hinting at the toxic venom it can unleash. Every step it takes sends a low metallic clang echoing, a dreadful warning to all who dare stand against it.

"The rules of combat aren’t fair sometimes... A dwarf like me has no business killing such a monster, but in the end, I must because it is necessary..." The spear in her hand started to give off a powerful spear aura.
"The current you can only handle 5% of my power... We can push past that when it comes down to it, but for now, only 5% can be accessed without you passing out," the Spear of Dawn spoke.
Camilla smiled, "I just need 2%."
One of the three souls hidden inside the spear has awakened, making the spear a terrifying killing tool. However, Camilla is still too weak to handle more than 5% of her true power.
But then again, Camilla doesn’t really need too much of a boost since she has more than enough means to fight a spirit Ascension stage spider.
So asking for 2% is even overkill. When the spider fully emerged from the forest, Camilla flew into the air, her hair blowing back in the gentle wind.
She was clad in lightweight whitish-silver armor. The Spear of Dawn was pulsing with energy so potent that when she pointed it at the spider, it felt its body grow heavier.
Its movement slowed down and eventually came to a halt.
"Starfall Lance."
The moment she muttered, a giant spear, about 15 meters long, appeared in the air. It was made of pure star energy, infused with spear qi.

The spider was locked down when the spear appeared, to the shock of Kent and Vexthra, who were watching from afar. Camilla stabbed her spear forward with one hand, and just like that, the giant spear in the air shot out, impaling the spider to the ground.
It couldn’t even raise its 20-meter-long metallic legs to defend itself. The spears went through its body, pinning it to the ground.
Camilla shook her head and flew away, joining the thick of the battle... It was rather unfortunate that the spider couldn’t withstand the 2% willpower of her spear.
Kent smiled slightly. "That is just cheating... Having a weapon spirit is just cheating."
Vexthra smiled slightly. "It is common to have weapon spirits. You will start seeing more of them in the higher worlds."

Kent smirked, but he couldn’t deny the fact that he also wanted a weapon spirit. Watching how Camilla easily destroyed the Ascension stage spider made him wonder just what she could do when she started using more of the weapon’s power.
Vexthra studied Kent’s expression for a few seconds and said, "You should probably get yourself a weapon spirit. It helps when comprehending your Sword Realm.
"But aside from that, in the Higher Worlds, where everything is competitive, you will meet swordsmen far more impressive than you are. Some will be enemies who wouldn’t blink at attacking you.
"So, having a weapon spirit to back you up will be great. Trust me, I know how valuable weapon spirits can be."
Kent turned and grabbed Vexthra by the waist, pulling her closer. "Do you have a weapon spirit?"
"I do. However, she is away exploring the Universe," Vexthra replied, making Kent look at her with a stunned expression.
"Weapon spirits can move on their own?" he asked.
"Yes. But not all can do that. My weapon spirit was once a Supreme who died during the primordial era. I researched her and found out she was known as the Wandering Bow Queen.
"So you see that even in death, she couldn’t help wandering around on her own..." Kent smiled, knowing something new about his first wife.
"So you are an Archeress, huh?" he smiled, making Vexthra blush slightly.
"I can also use the sword. In fact, I was once a sword immortal but had to let go of one and ascend with the other. It was a big moment for me, but eventually I dropped the sword and took the bow."
"So, do you like to have a title... like your weapon spirit, who is called the Wandering Bow Queen?" Kent asked, but Vexthra’s blush deepened, and she planted her face in Kent’s chest.
"I-I won’t tell you."
Kent smiled, knowing full well she would tell him eventually. But for now, he decided to tease her, so he gently kneaded her butt, making the goddess blush even more deeply.
"Hey, lovebirds, some of us are actually doing something useful, so perhaps take your lovemaking elsewhere."
Unity said with a giggle, casting a knowing smile at Kent and Vexthra. The two of them blushed and decided to pay closer attention to the battle.
However, the few moments shared just now continued to bring a smile to Kent’s face.
Vexthra was the same.
Moments like this were all she wanted.

To spend time with her man, regardless of how limited it was. Spending time with her sisters, sharing mortal stories, and even going as far as spending time with the humans and the Bloodveins in the tower...
She was once a mortal, but now, as a goddess, she had forgotten what it felt like to be mortal, so she was relearning everything...

Thankfully, her man has more than enough people around him to help her. So aside from the sex, she just wanted to spend some time in her man’s arms as they watched mortals fight against monstrous beasts.

chapters.title: Chapter 692: First Floor Battle (3)
paragraphs: On the first floating island, Nara, Lani, Elaine, Val, Vaelros, Khaazal, Gorzak, Zharkaz, and Yi Lai were clearing there. The team-up wasn’t in any particular order. Kent just wanted them to test their strength and see where they must improve, since the first floor was easy enough.
Their side was also dealing with the same type of spiders as the ones Unity’s team was handling on the middle floating island.

It wasn’t necessary, but Nara decided to ride her Hellhorse in battle today. She sat on the terrifying horse, whose body had become almost metal, perhaps bony, with green hellfire burning through the sockets of its eyes.
The moment Nara sat on the Hellhorse, her eyes turned green like the color of the flames, and her two swords were engulfed in flames. As she moved, green flames trailed her.
The Hellhorse was doing all the movements, so all she was doing was swinging her swords, killing and immobilizing as many as she could.

The number of spiders she was immobilizing was higher than the number she was killing. This was because, just like the predicament Vari found herself in, Lani, being an assassin, faced the same dilemma.
However, since Nara was creating the chances, all she was doing was going for the kill. Of course, she could use her scythe, just like how Vari didn’t use hers.
Seeing this as an easy battle, she was using the daggers, honing her skills for when she would truly find herself at a disadvantage, where even her scythe would be useless.
However, Elaine was doing better than one might think. She wasn’t using her death abilities. Instead, she wielded two swords.
One of the swords was white and the other was black.

One might expect a healer to use mage-like skills to kill, but Elaine was doing the opposite. When she awakened her Primordial spirit, the aspect of her that was once known as the Contractor had awakened.
The Contractor was recognized as one of the greatest killers in the history of the universe. That part of her uses the sword, and while she is not a swordswoman per se, she qualifies to become one.
She was dual-wielding, and judging by the speed at which she was moving and killing, it was clear her understanding of the swords was on another level.

As for Val, she was just whooshing through the forest, emitting potent Lunar energy. It was as if the moon goddess had descended upon the space, and given the number of spiders she had already killed, it was safe to say things were going remarkably well for her.
Vaelros was also killing with his Chains of Torment, and Khaazal, the wyvern, wasn’t falling behind either. He wielded his spear, wind gushing out as he moved across the battlefield.
Gorzak, Zharkaz, and Yi Lai were equally stunning on the battlefield. They didn’t seem to be in any difficult situation at all.
Eventually, they were nearing the completion of their battle. Meanwhile, the battles on Islands 2 and 3 had already come to an end.
Island 2 was handled by Lilian, Vari, Zaila, Princess Lovina, Zareth, Nykali, Veera, and Volthar. Their team was just too robust.
When the battle started, Zaila used ’Mind Shock’ on hundreds of the spiders, and Princess Lovina unleashed her poison.
It was a well-coordinated and straightforward attack that brought the spiders’ demise much faster. The two only saved a few for Vari to use as target practice.
In the meantime, Nykali only collected the souls, and Veera raised the dead spiders to become cannon fodder until they leave the dungeon.
She has different classes of undead, so she deemed these spiders cannon fodder. Her primary targets were the floor bosses. They were the ones she wanted to add to her undead legion.

As for Island 3, Selene, Velyra, Neomi, Mara, Elsa, Sylara, Aetheris, Kazarak, and Ankaara handled it. The battle started slowly at first, but the moment blood started pouring on the battlefield, things became much more mesmerizing.
Velyra, whose control over blood is rather high, started to kill much faster, using the blood of the slain as an extension of her sword.
She was shaping the blood to do more than immobilize. To some degree, she was able to tap into the blood inside the wounded spiders and kill them from within.

Though the spiders don’t have the same blood as some beasts or humans, the liquid within them responded to every command Velyra gave, and, like her allies, the blood was what she depended on for most of the kills.

However, she wasn’t the only one who used the blood to her advantage. Sylara also exploited it to her advantage. At first, she had to drink it to gain energy, but this time, just being around it was enough to give her the same effect.
She merely used the blood to coat her claws, and the rest was history.
The Neomi also lived up to her name as the mother of killers. With so much death happening around her, she became much more deadly. Even after the battle ended, she felt like joining in again.
However, by the time they arrived at the second island, the battle had also ended. Then she went to the first, but that place too had ended the fight.
But when they arrived at the middle island, the battle was ending. She quickly joined in to handle the rest.
*Screeeeeech*
Suddenly, a screeching sound came from deep within the forest. "The Floor boss is coming... Hahaha," Kaizo’s voice boomed, readying himself for a good battle.
However, his dreams were shattered the moment the Floor boss, towering 30 meters tall, appeared, when a soft voice suddenly entered everyone’s ear.
"Blossom Feisty Unity Arrow."
A sleek, rainbow-like arrow streaked through the air, entering one of the ten eyes on the Floor Boss, ending its existence before it could show its true powers.
It didn’t even get to show how monstrous it is.
Unity giggled, putting away her bow as she gazed at Kaizo and her sisters, who clearly wanted to have a go at the spider monstrosity she had just taken down.
Unity may not look like it, but just like how she can be quiet, innocent, and calm like Blossom, she can also be annoying like Feisty.
Kent and Vexthra flew down, landing beside the ladies, who immediately surrounded him.
⟦Congratulations on clearing the first floor of the Planet Killer Dungeon. Rewards have been deposited into your tower storage⟧

chapters.title: Chapter 693: Great Rewards
paragraphs: "Unity, what is the name of the arrow you just used?" Kaizo asked, looking at the young lady who stole his kill.
Kaizo knew it was his time to shine, yet it ended with Unity sending her arrow through the eye of the Peak Spirit Ascension spider.
Now, all he could ask for was the name of the arrow that managed to reach the Floor Boss without it even noticing.
Unity smiled and opened her palm, causing an arrow to appear. It looked like it had been formed from a rainbow, considering it encompassed every color in existence.

"It is called Blossom Feisty Unity Arrow," Unity said with an embarrassed expression. The sisters just chuckled. It wasn’t hard to tell that the naming wasn’t her idea, but rather that of her Primordial Spirits—most specifically, Feisty’s.
After all, Blossom, her second primordial spirit, created it...
Alina took the arrow and studied it for a few seconds before nodding. "This is a work of art. It doesn’t contain any runes, but it is already enough to handle something like the spider."
She looked at Unity, a smile forming on her lips. "How many of these can you produce?"
"As many as you want, provided I have enough energy." Alina nodded cheerfully.
"I have an Augmentation Array that can turn these arrows into Spirit Lord-worthy killing arrows. If you want, I can start with the first 100."
Unity nodded and created 100 Blossom Feisty Unity Arrows. Since Alina needed something to be busy with, she might as well earn something from it.
Alina smiled and directly sent everything to her grid space. Kaizo knew this wouldn’t be the last time Unity stole his last kill, so he started planning his revenge.
The rivalry between Unity and Kaizo had just begun.
Kent suspected something like that, but he knew it would be a harmless rivalry, so he said nothing. Instead, he turned to the system to examine the rewards and their usage.
After looking around for a while, Kent took out a vial containing an elixir, unclung it, and gulped it down. The moment he did, he felt his bones growing stronger.
"Good stuff." A smile appeared on his face. He took out another and showed it to his legion and wives.

"This is the Eternal Steel Bone Tempering Elixir... drinking it will have some effect on your bones. Take it as a bonus for clearing the first floor." Kent unclung the elixir and poured it into Vexthra’s mouth.
Though it would probably have little to no effect on her, the rewards inside his tower storage included her, so she might as well drink it.

"You can check your space rings for yours." They all checked and took them out, drinking everything immediately. When they did, the feeling of strength coursed through their bodies, making them smile.
Afterwards, Kent gave the Serpent Breath Poison recipe to Princess Lovina, who was more than happy to receive something aside from the elixir.
The next thing Kent brought out was the Map of the Planet Killer Dungeon. It is a device that, the moment he channeled his energy into it, displayed a detailed map of the four floating islands.

"This map will guide you in exploring the island. It features detailed landmarks that make it easy to find something interesting inside the dungeon. I don’t have much time to waste on it, but since we have 12 years to clear this dungeon, you guys can spend some days exploring it.
The map of the second floor will be added after you clear it. So, for now, you can explore this floor before heading to the second floor."
They nodded. Twelve years may sound like a long time, but it will be over soon, so they knew they had to get things going fast before they ran out of time.
"One last thing... Neomi, Selene, Kazarak, and Zharkaz, look into your space rings." The four did as they were told. Neomi pulled out a sleek red key, and the rest pulled out small golden orbs.

"Selene, Kazarak, and Zharkaz, crush your orbs." These are the drops received after clearing the first floor. The tower automatically sent everything into the tower space, and then, using a few tower points, Gaia directed the orbs to their intended recipients.
Selene, Kazarak, and Zharkaz did as they were told, and each received a golden key.

"What you have in your hands are keys that will unlock your memories." Kent looked at Kazarak and Zharkaz. "You two will receive fragments of your memories. It may be a sad or a happy memory, so prepare before using it."
Kent then turned to Selene and Neomi. "You two must be wondering what type of memories you will be unlocking after all your memories are intact.

The answer is simple: every last one of you, regardless of your background, was once someone great. Most of you died defending your family, some died defending their worlds, and some died defending the universe.
However, while you were meant to be dead and remain dead, some idiot did something brilliant years ago, and due to that, you now have a second chance at life.
I don’t know what these memories will do, but whatever you see, treat them as yours, for they are indeed yours—memories of the life you lived billions of years ago."
By the time Kent was done, everyone around him remained quiet... the sheer shock they felt was enough to show they were indeed gobsmacked.
"No need to look shocked... You are bound to remember one of these days, so getting it this early isn’t too bad."
Kent made sure everyone calmed down before he continued with the rest of what he had to say. He would be leaving soon, so he wanted to make sure everyone had what they needed.
The four with the memory keys also decided to hold on to them for now until they all received a key. This way, they could all use them at the same time.
Kent was okay with that, so he let them have their way. After he was done with everything, they decided to start exploring the four floating islands.
"You have to leave, Kent. We have everything under control, so don’t worry about us..." Vexthra said, resting in Kent’s arms.
"Though we will miss you, the mission is also important, so go now while you still have time."
Kent nodded. After kissing all his ladies, he left the dungeon and went back to the tower.

chapters.title: Chapter 694: The Black Sea [Bonus]
paragraphs: The moment Kent got back to the tower, he quickly used it to harness one of the markers he had placed on its tether.
He was going to the Half-Elves kingdom, and the shortest path was via the Black Sea, so he used the tether he had left when he and his wives took down the Sect Master of the Divine Palace sect.
Back then, Kent and Kaizo chased him down and gave him a rather great beating. What he did to Nara and Zaila was too inhuman, so they reminded him of that through beatings.
Thankfully, his ladies also came and added to his suffering. So, when all was done back then, Kent used the tower to leave a marker, allowing him to teleport there in the future.
The battle happened near the Black Sea. So he left the marker there.
Coincidentally, he would need the marker today since the shortest path to the Elven land was through the Black Sea.
They said crossing it was the last thing anyone wanted to do. But Kent knew that if he were to go through the Ancient Battlefield of Parting, it would take weeks before he arrived at his destination.
In fact, he knew that getting through the gateway, which led to the Elven lands, wasn’t going to be easy...
Of course, he could choose to kill those who would prevent him from passing. However, that would bring too much trouble for everyone.
So he would rather take the path where the danger had been stated, but it was also the fastest path to the Elven land.
Kent stood on a small mountain, gazing at the vast expanse of the sea stretching several miles away from him. "It goes without saying the sea is rather scary... however, it hasn’t met me yet."
Kent smiled.
The moment he moves, there will be no turning back.
Kent sighed and then retrieved a flying boat. "Per the map, if I travel 10,000 miles per hour, I will get to the shores of the Elf kingdoms within three days... it is too far, but I can only go now."
Kent made the flying boat float before him, and then he gently jumped in. Without even thinking, he channeled his energy into the boat, and it began to move.
The speed didn’t pick up early simply because Kent wanted to explore some things first, so he was moving slowly, though not too slowly.
"Shax said that to get a chance to register because I am a human, I must first prove myself worthy..." Kent smiled.

"I wonder if revealing myself as Kent would get me what I want. After all, everyone wants my head, so what better way to get popular than by revealing myself?" Kent had no intention of hiding his identity.
He knew one way or another, he would clash with all those who wanted him dead, so why not get it done now and be free from future troubles?
Vexthra made him aware that the moment he stepped into a High world, the competition would be much more severe. Countless geniuses were waiting for him out there...
Kent may have easily killed a Spirit King, but he might just find himself clashing on equal footing or even being suppressed by another Spirit King...
Naturally, that would be because the Spirit King had a much stronger foundation than the ones Kent easily killed. So, based on one’s foundation, the odds of battle would become much more severe.
However, Vexthra knew Kent was a monster, so she knew killing him would be next to impossible... Kent was basically the kind of monster whose potential was endless.

She knew that instead of hiding, Kent would probably be the one going around causing trouble. So she wasn’t worried. All she wanted was for Kent to compete with people who could give him a run for his money.

Getting good competition would be great for Kent. This is why he planned on using his real self to handle things. He wouldn’t want to hide when he could stand at the peak and not fear for his own life.
There were indeed more harrowing dangers in the world, but Kent was not an easy target. If he wanted, he could just bring the entire world under his control using his legion.

"So I have to get to the Half-Elves Kingdom in the next five days if I want to be on time to register for the competition. Also, the likelihood that they will prevent me from registering is high, so I must prepare for that too."
Kent smiled weakly and sighed. "The Hand got angry this time, so they are going all out."
Shax, the shadow demon, had already reported to him that the Hand had spread word again that whoever kills Kent will receive great wealth.
And if that wasn’t enticing enough—considering anything from the Hand is of great value—they also promised to give the demons an Ascension platform if they manage to kill him.
So while sending out an entire demon race after him seemed shameless, the demons wanted an Ascension platform. And since they were desperate, they would consider coming after him.

"What a headache... Vexthra made me promise her I wouldn’t cause too much trouble for the demons, simply because she is also a demon. She said, although it may seem that demons are superior in most High and Immortal worlds, the truth is that humans and other races suppress them.
So she didn’t want her people to feel suppressed in this world, too." Kent scratched the back of his head. "Not that I have any problem with the demons..."

If he had to tell the truth, his plans for going to the other continents were for experience, so he never truly wanted to suppress or slaughter anybody. But when they attacked him, he would have to fight back.
This meant now that the demons were gearing up to go after him, the chances of him doing what his wife was afraid of were just high...
This placed Kent in a complicated state. However, after a moment’s thought, he realized that even if they attacked him, putting them on the right path was also an option.
"Chaos would have slaughtered them all... but I am Kent, the correct version of me, so I will break their legs and arms and perhaps their teeth."

But when they attacked him, he would have to fight back.
This meant now that the demons were gearing up to go after him, the chances of him doing what his wife was afraid of were just high...
This placed Kent in a complicated state.
However, after a moment’s thought, he realized that even if they attacked him, putting them on the right path was also an option.
"Chaos would have slaughtered them all... but I am Kent, the correct version of me, so I will break their legs and arms and perhaps their teeth."

chapters.title: Chapter 695: Sea Monsters [Bonus]
paragraphs: A day had passed since Kent left the human continent for the Elf Kingdom.
At the moment, he was moving very fast, and while he knew there was danger lurking within the sea, he didn’t really care much about that.
The speed he was going was fast enough to get to his destination without much trouble. So he just sat in a meditative posture and continued to feel the serene environment around him.
A few hours later, Vexthra reached out to him...
[Vexthra, my love, are you missing me already?] Kent asked the moment he heard Vexthra’s voice in his head.
Vexthra smirked, standing at the edge of the middle floating island, inside the dungeon. "Nobody misses you. So just focus on your mission."
[Ouch... that hurts, Vex... very hurtful.] Kent smiled and asked why she contacted him.
"We managed to explore every last detail on the map, but we only found something small. One was a spirit grape tree that had some powerful, soul-nourishing grape fruits, over 10,000 years old.

I transplanted three inside the Love Garden and five in the Mountain Garden with the help of the tower, and left the rest inside the dungeon. Also, I left a couple of hundred grapes in the Tower Storage."
[That is a good one then.] Kent smiled.

"Yes. However, the second thing we discovered is related to Unity. It turns out Blossom was once the goddess of Love. We don’t know much, but it was much more apparent considering how Unity reacted to this information."
[How did she react to it?]
"Well, first, the language the texts were written in was one only she recognized, despite not knowing she could read or speak that language."
Additionally, after translating the writings, which were akin to a diary of the Goddess of Love, Unity felt as though she was there, experiencing everything firsthand.
It was weird, but after reading everything, it became something akin to a...
[Memory]

"Yes. It was just a few bits of memory, but it turns out that just that can make her gain more than she expected. Her Primordial spirit, whom we named Blossom, gained additional gifts she could use to help strengthen Unity.
It was just too strange how a memory could have made such a change in a person." Vexthra was both happy and shocked when Unity gained a bit of her memory.
She knew this was the turning point for her sister, so she was happy for her but also shocked that the memory had been able to cause such a significant change.

Kent, on the other hand, was just smiling as the flying boat sped across the Black Sea. Though its name was exaggerated at the outer sections, as he moved further from the shores, the sea indeed got darker by the passing hours.
So its name, the Black Sea, was indeed warranted.
[Just make sure that as more memories are discovered, she doesn’t hastily divulge everything to her sisters. It may not seem like much, but revealing too much about one’s past can be dangerous.]
"I made her aware..." Vexthra responded, and Kent nodded.
[Then keep looking for more clues for her. The moment I get a way to awaken her true name, I won’t hesitate to do it.
Also, the eight new undead will be ready in two weeks, so for now, keep doing what you deem necessary and don’t rush to go through the floors.]
"We won’t rush. Now that we know Unity has more to gain in the dungeons, we will be taking our time to see how much we can help her."
[Great... then I will talk to you later... I have incoming.]
"Okay... have fun."
Kent narrowed his gaze at the swarm of monsters swimming after him and toward him.
"Looks like the sea monsters don’t want me to pass." He wasn’t even done when a large shark with metallic teeth lunged at him.
Kent’s sword appeared, and with a quick swing, the shark was cut in half, sending it crashing back into the water, instantly changing its color to red.
But it wasn’t the only monster that attacked. Kent immediately found himself surrounded from all sides, forcing him to slow down the flying boat.

"A good day to farm tower points and Soul Essence." With a smile on his face, he started killing the sea monsters. They weren’t that strong. Most were at the Root Transcendent stage, so he was basically bullying them.
However, coming in large numbers was both to Kent’s advantage and disadvantage. His advantage is that he will get to farm more Tower Points and Soul essence.
But bad for him because he allowed them to get closer. If he is not quick and powerful enough, he will be overwhelmed.
And as the minutes passed and stronger ones started appearing, Kent had to abandon his boat, sending it into the tower space, and chose to fly on his own.

This made it much more convenient to kill, and he was doing just that. His level 2 Sword Qi and Intent were active, so even the monsters that managed to slip through his attack couldn’t get within a meter of him without being shredded to meat paste.

After attaining the four sword enlightenments, Kent’s Profound Sword Qi and Intent had become much more potent. He was using just the sword qi with the intent to kill dozens of monsters, as if it were the most normal thing to do.
Within ten minutes, Kent had killed thousands of sea monsters, and more continued to come. Not that he was complaining, considering every single kill was giving him something he needed.
The tower points and the soul essence were flooding in per kill, so he was having a rather great field trip even if he had to abandon his ship.
One hour later, the Black Sea within a 10-mile radius had become the Red Sea, and that was when Kent knew the true danger was coming.

Of course, he felt it, far from him. He felt something or somebody locked their murderous gaze on him. It didn’t take long for him to see who wanted him dead by sending tens of thousands of monsters to their death.
"A sea dragon," Kent smirked, watching the dragon move at a terrifying speed toward him.
"Maybe I should get a sea dragon to help me cross the sea next time." Kent smiled and then locked gazes with the colossal dragon, who quickly appeared, splashing water on Kent.
