chapters.title: Chapter 696: Sea Guardian [Bonus]
paragraphs: The water splashed, and before reaching Kent, every last droplet turned into a pointed needle capable of piercing the strongest metal. However, Kent just hovered in the air, defending everything with his sword energy.
When the attack cleared, his gaze fell on the blue-scaled water dragon. It was about 150 meters long, its massive serpentine body coiling within the water.

Its scales shimmered like polished sapphires, reflecting the dim light with an almost hypnotic glow. Jagged fins ran along its spine, rippling as it moved, and its deep, glowing eyes locked onto Kent with fierce intelligence.
Water vapor swirled around it, misting the air as they locked in a fierce gaze.
Water dragons don’t have wings, but they make do with their long bodies. They are more like overgrown sea serpents, but much more dangerous, especially when fighting on their home turf.
"Hello there... You wouldn’t happen to know which direction leads to the Elven kingdom?" Kent asked with a smile, disregarding the fact that he had just been attacked.
The dragon didn’t respond; instead, its eyes turned a deep blue, and the water around it began to boil. Kent felt a powerful pressure coming from the water, causing him to move back.
However, before he could get too far, a vortex rose from the surface of the water and started pulling him in.
His body felt like it had no choice but to enter the vortex. However, Kent knew doing so would be a disaster, so he held his ground.
After a few seconds, seeing Kent wasn’t getting pulled into the vortex, the dragon struck with its tail, sending a wide arc of water at Kent.
Kent’s eyes narrowed as the powerful water arc surged toward him, roaring with the force of a crashing wave.
He tightened his grip on his sword, gathering his sword energy into a shimmering barrier that flickered like liquid light.
The water slammed against the barrier, sending ripples and splashes outward, but it held firm. Not even a crack appeared on it.
’That was powerful...’
The dragon coiled its massive body, its tail whipping back for another strike. Kent leapt into the air, dodging the second arc with precise timing.
He could feel the raw energy of the dragon’s attack vibrating through the air, each strike designed to overwhelm and crush.
’...This is interesting... Unlike the other Core Formation experts who had formed and refined their cores seven times, this dragon has the strength to back his cultivation base.’
Kent was intrigued, finding even more reason to explore the world beyond the human continent.
’Looks like this trip won’t be wasted.’
Hovering above the churning waters, Kent focused, weaving his sword energy into a sharp, radiant blade that extended far beyond the physical blade of his sword.
With a sudden burst, he launched himself forward, aiming to pierce through the swirling vortex and land a decisive blow.
The water dragon roared, unleashing a spray of boiling water and a surge of pressure that threatened to knock Kent off course.
But Kent’s sword intent flared, cutting through the tempest like a beacon of calm in the storm. The vortex was extinguished just like that.
This gave Kent a few moments of calm, so he scanned the dragon.
⟦Name: Thalorin Abysswalker⟧
⟦Bloodline: Tidal Sovereign Bloodline (unawakened)⟧
⟦Race: Ancient Sea Race⟧
⟦Realm: Core Formation (7/7)⟧
⟦Title: Outer Sea Guardian of the Sea Race⟧
Kent read the info with a calm expression. He had already suspected the guardian Shax spoke of was this dragon, so he wasn’t shocked or anything.
"At this moment, if you have even a trace of a brain, you should know there is no way you will be able to kill me... so why don’t we talk like normal people?"
Kent proposed, looking at the dragon, who said nothing despite Kent knowing he could talk and even take on a humanoid form. He wasn’t a typical monster — he was a dragon, after all.
This meant he could talk, yet so far, Kent could only see the fury in the dragon’s eyes.
"They came at me, and I killed them... it was self-defense," Kent smiled. "If anything, you should blame yourself for sending those weak monsters at me."

He saw that the anger came from the fact that he had slaughtered every last sea monster sent his way. So he addressed that, and while he didn’t want to show it, he knew the dragon was planning an attack.
But Kent wasn’t worried. The worst that could happen was that he would finally kill his first dragon and continue his journey.
"Who are you?" Suddenly, the dragon spoke, causing Kent to smile.
"So you can talk, yet you choose to fight instead. Dragons..." Kent shook his head.
"You, sir... You can call me Kent Madson. Nice meeting you." The moment he introduced himself, the atmosphere became tense.
The attack the dragon was preparing failed, but it managed to hold onto it, gazing intensely at Kent like he was some monster.
Among the many things the dragon had encountered at sea, it had never prepared for the one person everyone was searching for.
Kent Madson—the name he was specifically ordered to stop from passing over the sea—was now right in front of him, and he couldn’t do anything to him.
Why couldn’t he do anything to Kent?
It was because, despite the tense atmosphere that shrouded the place due to Kent revealing his name, the dragon saw that he was just smiling with his defense down, not even considering him a threat.
The dragon was not an idiot—he knew Kent wasn’t acting. The confidence oozing from the brat was enough to tell him the human before him was dangerous.
However, he was also in a dilemma.
He had been given strict orders to take down or restrain the human named Kent Madson if he were to encounter him.
But as it stood, the mighty Sea Dragon—Outer Guardian of the Sea Race—knew deep in his draconic heart that he didn’t have what it took to restrain Kent, let alone kill him.
This put him in a state that made him start to wonder which road to take.

chapters.title: Chapter 697: Sending A Message
paragraphs: The Sea Dragon was put in an unfavorable situation by Kent.
From the moment the Hand sent a message to the leaders of the Sea Race, he was ordered to stop anyone named Kent Madson at all costs.
They emphasized that he could kill Kent Madson or restrain him. They also warned him that under no circumstances should he be allowed to pass.
He couldn’t fail... That was just not acceptable.
However, it was plain as day now that Kent wouldn’t be going down... not when the Sea Dragon didn’t have backup.
So watching the smile on Kent’s face left him angrier than ever, yet he was powerless to do anything.
"Since you now know my name, then why don’t I say what I have to say..." Kent sighed. Killing the Dragon would be a waste. Kent isn’t some bloodthirsty maniac who goes about killing for fun.
He knew the dragon was ordered... so if anyone deserved to die, it should be the ones doing the ordering. It shouldn’t even have anything to do with the dragon.
But that doesn’t mean the dragon was free from further actions from Kent. If anything, it meant the dragon’s life and death were in his own hands. Depending on what he did, Kent would answer.

"I know the Hand has already told you about me... Everything they said is true and then some. But what they failed to tell you was that I have what it takes to bring your entire race to their knees in under three minutes.
And this is not a brag. I can do it, and I know deep down you know I can do it. So save yourself this time because I was hoping you could send a message to your people."
Thalorin, the Sea Dragon, looked at Kent for a few minutes before its body shuddered. The waves rose, and a searing heat came from the boiling water.
I guess threatening his race didn’t seem right to him. Kent moved to the side, evading a water spear fashioned into a long and deadly weapon.
More of such weapons appeared, but Kent dodged and destroyed as many as he could. It wasn’t as much of a headache as one might think, but Kent had indeed shown Thalorin he wasn’t afraid of him.
If anything, it was the dragon’s pride that was dragging it into a frenzied state, one where it didn’t want to take a moment and rethink its approach.
At the moment, blinded by loyalty, he wanted to use that misguided loyalty to accomplish the task. But that was just some stupid way of thinking.

Thalorin’s eyes flared with a blazing blue light as the boiling waves churned violently around him. With a deafening roar, the Sea Dragon unleashed his first deadly skill: Tidal Fury, a colossal surge of water that slammed toward Kent like a raging tsunami.
Kent’s body moved with fluid grace, dodging and weaving through the crashing waves as if he were part of the storm itself.
Kent didn’t even attack the dragon; instead, he chose to evade its attacks, which continued to come.
Thalorin growled in frustration, then gathered the swirling storm above his massive form, summoning his second skill: Inferno Maelstrom.
Flames erupted amid the watery tempest, mixing fire and water into a deadly storm of scalding steam and crackling lightning bolts that sizzled through the air.
Kent’s body flickered into a series of afterimages, each one striking the edges of the maelstrom, dispersing the storm’s energy with precise bursts of Rapid Slash.
Thalorin roared once more and summoned his ultimate skill: Leviathan’s Wrath, a massive spectral dragon made of pure ocean energy, appeared and crashed down with crushing force.
However, despite the distance between them not being that wide, Kent merely used the Void Cleave to handle one of the strongest skills of the dragon.
The sword skill that requires distance to gather momentum was handled just like that.
"Though I have to say this dragon is stronger... it is just that I am not normal," Kent smiled, evading one attack after another.
"I should probably add my points and break the next limit," Kent thought while also wondering why the dragon was struggling to comprehend what was happening.
All the attacks he was throwing at Kent were being dealt with, yet he continued to be stubborn.
After an hour, he stopped attacking and transformed into a blue-haired young man who seemed to be in his 40s. He had two elegant dragon horns on his forehead and a fine, muscular physique.
A spear appeared in his hand, and he was about to attack when Kent moved and appeared before him, landing a punch on his face.
The force from the punch was so powerful that the dragon was sent flying into the air and then landed with a heavy thud inside the water.
His left eye turned black thanks to Kent’s fist.
"Look, don’t be blinded by your loyalty to the Sea Race. I have already planned on not killing you, so maybe stop pushing my hand. I might become angry now and actually kill you.

And while that will be a bummer, know that I have someone who can turn you into an undead, which in this case, you wouldn’t have a say in whether you listen to what I have to say or not." The words left Kent’s lips casually.
The black-eyed dragon, who heard Kent’s words seethe in anger, however, was unable to do anything. He had already seen Kent’s strength, and that terrified him.
"Very well... Looks like you have calmed down now," Kent smiled and then started saying what he wanted to say an hour ago.
"I want you to send a message to your leaders... Tell them I don’t want a conflict with them, that I only want to ask them a few questions about events that happened years ago.

Be sure to say precisely these words: ’I have a way to break the Wynthralls’ curse.’ Saying that will calm them down. And if they don’t want to listen, you can give them this:" Kent threw a grape to the dragon.
He caught it, and after inspecting it for a few seconds, his eyes widened. Kent smiled.
"I will be going to places like the Dragon Kingdom or the Dwarf Kingdom after I am done with my business in the Elf Kingdom. So if you want to talk to me, meet me then.
That will be all. Again, be sure to tell them they don’t want to become my enemy... They wouldn’t want to know what I will do."
With that, Kent flew away.

If anything, it was the dragon’s pride that was dragging it into a frenzied state, one where it didn’t want to take a moment and rethink its approach.
At the moment, blinded by loyalty, he wanted to use that misguided loyalty to accomplish the task.
But that was just some stupid way of thinking.
Thalorin’s eyes flared with a blazing blue light as the boiling waves churned violently around him.
With a deafening roar, the Sea Dragon unleashed his first deadly skill: Tidal Fury, a colossal surge of water that slammed toward Kent like a raging tsunami.
Kent’s body moved with fluid grace, dodging and weaving through the crashing waves as if he were part of the storm itself.
Kent didn’t even attack the dragon; instead, he chose to evade its attacks, which continued to come.
Thalorin growled in frustration, then gathered the swirling storm above his massive form, summoning his second skill: Inferno Maelstrom.
Flames erupted amid the watery tempest, mixing fire and water into a deadly storm of scalding steam and crackling lightning bolts that sizzled through the air.
Kent’s body flickered into a series of afterimages, each one striking the edges of the maelstrom, dispersing the storm’s energy with precise bursts of Rapid Slash.
Thalorin roared once more and summoned his ultimate skill: Leviathan’s Wrath, a massive spectral dragon made of pure ocean energy, appeared and crashed down with crushing force.
However, despite the distance between them not being that wide, Kent merely used the Void Cleave to handle one of the strongest skills of the dragon.
The sword skill that requires distance to gather momentum was handled just like that.
"Though I have to say this dragon is stronger... it is just that I am not normal," Kent smiled, evading one attack after another.
"I should probably add my points and break the next limit," Kent thought while also wondering why the dragon was struggling to comprehend what was happening.
All the attacks he was throwing at Kent were being dealt with, yet he continued to be stubborn.
After an hour, he stopped attacking and transformed into a blue-haired young man who seemed to be in his 40s.
He had two elegant dragon horns on his forehead and a fine, muscular physique.
A spear appeared in his hand, and he was about to attack when Kent moved and appeared before him, landing a punch on his face.
The force from the punch was so powerful that the dragon was sent flying into the air and then landed with a heavy thud inside the water.
His left eye turned black thanks to Kent’s fist.
"Look, don’t be blinded by your loyalty to the Sea Race.
I have already planned on not killing you, so maybe stop pushing my hand.
I might become angry now and actually kill you.

And while that will be a bummer, know that I have someone who can turn you into an undead, which in this case, you wouldn’t have a say in whether you listen to what I have to say or not." The words left Kent’s lips casually.
The black-eyed dragon, who heard Kent’s words seethe in anger, however, was unable to do anything.
He had already seen Kent’s strength, and that terrified him.
"Very well...
Looks like you have calmed down now," Kent smiled and then started saying what he wanted to say an hour ago.
"I want you to send a message to your leaders...
Tell them I don’t want a conflict with them, that I only want to ask them a few questions about events that happened years ago.
Be sure to say precisely these words: ’I have a way to break the Wynthralls’ curse.’ Saying that will calm them down.
And if they don’t want to listen, you can give them this:" Kent threw a grape to the dragon.
He caught it, and after inspecting it for a few seconds, his eyes widened.
Kent smiled.
"I will be going to places like the Dragon Kingdom or the Dwarf Kingdom after I am done with my business in the Elf Kingdom.
So if you want to talk to me, meet me then.
That will be all.
Again, be sure to tell them they don’t want to become my enemy...
They wouldn’t want to know what I will do."
With that, Kent flew away.

chapters.title: Chapter 698: Breaking The Soul and Mind Limit
paragraphs: "So you made contact with one of the ancient races," Vexthra asked, now seated on a clean white stone on the first island.
[Yes. Thalorin is a good guy. I think we are now friends—at least from my perspective, we are friends.] Kent responded with a smile.
Vexthra rolled her eyes. "Unbelievable... Only you would think that after fighting a dragon, you would automatically become friends."
After Kent resumed his journey, now back inside his sleek flying boat, he reached out to Vexthra, who was still exploring the first floor of the Planet Killer Dungeon.

After they discovered the dungeon had something Unity needed, they chose to remain there for a few days to see if they could help her more. The map helped them find one, so they wanted to know if they could discover more secrets that might benefit Unity.
They were yet to make headway, but they weren’t giving up.
"So, how long until you reach the shores of the Elf Kingdom?" Vexthra asked.
[At this speed, a day and a half, maybe...]
"Okay... Let me know when you get there," Kent nodded and cut the connection. He wanted to do something else while he had some free time.
He quickly checked his profile to see how many attribute points he had racked up.
⟦Attribute Points: 1795⟧
A smile appeared on his lips. The birthday celebration with his wives had gone quite well for him, considering he had racked up this many attribute points.
Since his profile had changed, even adding one point to his attributes seemed to bring about so much change in his body that he hadn’t yet come to terms with it.
But it was now plain as day what had to be done to break a limit, and he knew the attribute points were now better than before.
Initially, he had to earn millions of points to break a limit, but now, just one point translates to thousands of points if converted to the previous system.
⟦Name: Kent⟧
⟦Bloodline: Primordial Chaos Dragon (16)⟧
⟦Class: Alchemist (Grandmaster)⟧
↠ SubClass
⟦Swordsman: (Grandmaster)⟧
⟦Soul Cultivation: (Tier 13)⟧
⟦Body Cultivator: (Diamond)⟧
⟦Cultivation: Core Formation - Lvl 3/9⟧
⟦Physique: 42/100⟧
⟦Spirit: 67/100⟧
"91 points more to break the next limit," Kent smiled and then ordered the tower to add the points. The moment the points were added, Kent’s body, mind, and soul felt the change immediately.
It was so overwhelming and enticing to the point that the moment the points were added, he wanted to punch a hole in the planet.
Obviously, he wasn’t going to do that.
"This feeling is intoxicating," Kent smiled.
Already, he could sense his soul had started to undergo some drastic changes. Changes that were making him feel like his understanding of the ’Soul Universe’ was limited.
The more the minutes passed, the more he felt like his soul was much more than he had let on. It was like his understanding was expanding, and that alone made him very happy.
As the hours went by, Kent’s understanding of the soul path he was following entered a stage that made him smile cheerfully.

"Instead of starting with an asteroid, I could have just started with something simpler yet deadly when used in battle, something like a large diamond. That would have consumed less Soul Essence." Kent scratched the back of his neck.
The Foxkin were feeding him Soul Essence every second, but that just wasn’t enough to create something as big as an asteroid capable of killing an immortal... he was far from that junction.
So if he had known there were some hidden methods in the path he was following, he would have done that.
Just now, he was enlightened to the fact that it didn’t even have to be an asteroid or a large diamond. It could be a water body, such as a pond, if you must.
But something simple that wouldn’t require too much Soul Essence would have gone a long way, especially when he was still in a medium world. But it was already too late.

He had started his asteroid project, and since he wanted to see it through, he could only hope he wouldn’t waste his energy and Soul Essence doing something foolish—all because he was fascinated by asteroids.
After a couple of hours, the process came to an end.
⟦Congratulations on breaking the 3rd limit on yourself: Soul Limit⟧
"So far, I broke a limit on my Body, Cultivation, and Soul... Looks like the next will be the mind." Kent was already aware that limits can be broken in four different places.
The Body limit relates to the person’s strength. Body cultivators who break a limit on their body become much more monstrous by all standards.

The Soul limit is mostly geared toward the strength of one’s soul. Soul Cultivators pursue these limits because breaking a soul limit not only strengthens one’s soul but also broadens their understanding of the soul path they are walking.
It helps them utilize their souls in ways they never knew possible.

The mind limit expands one’s mind, making it more robust, much like the soul. It enhances one’s mental strength and thinking ability. Essentially, the moment a mental limit is broken, one can expect a significant boost in their comprehension abilities.
The Cultivation limit breaks the limit on cultivation. The last three improve cultivation as well, but the main limitation on the cultivation path, when broken, enhances the cultivator’s potential.

Aspects like sword cultivation will see monumental growth, one that cannot be easily achieved. However, it isn’t just the sword path; all other aspects of cultivation will undergo significant changes.
Naturally, breaking a cultivation limit is much more difficult since its effects even affect the other three limits: mind, body, and soul.
But Kent had already broken that limit, and now he was done with his soul. He quickly checked the following requirements to determine which limit he would break next.
⟦Physique: 0/250⟧
⟦Spirit: 0/250⟧
⟦Tower Notice: Saturate both your ’Physique’ and ’Spirit’ to break your next limit: Mind Limit⟧
"Ah, what the hell... Tower, add the points, let me get my mind much sharper." Kent smiled. The next instant, his mind began to expand...
’Damn, I am a monster for sure now.’
The process took hours, but when it was done, Kent saw a huge change occur in his mind. It was a wild one, but he made progress, and that alone was all he wanted.
Checking the next requirements, he smiled slightly...
⟦Physique: 0/1050⟧
⟦Spirit: 0/1050⟧
⟦Tower Notice: Saturate both your ’Physique’ and ’Spirit’ to break your next limit: Soul Limit⟧

chapters.title: Chapter 699: The Enticing Offer [Bonus]
paragraphs: After the half-elves announced that there would be an open competition in a couple of months to select the five best candidates to enter the Flame Tower, many began preparing.
The Flame Tower is a place everyone would want to enter and cultivate flame art if they had the chance. However, for thousands of years, it has been a strict selection by the Lords and the King.

Of course, this means that even if you have the talent but haven’t caught the eyes of the King or the Lords, you wouldn’t be allowed entry. Those selected are mostly the children of a Lord or their friends.
Most wanted to join, but because of the strict requirements, they couldn’t even have a chance to try their luck. However, this year, things are different.
The announcement of the open competition ignited the flames in all those who had given up. This year, they get to try and see if they are destined to enter the Flame Tower.
All half-elves, both in their kingdom and outside, upon hearing this announcement, returned to take part in the competition that will commence in a few days.
Currently, inside Elarion, thousands of young half-elves are in line, registering for a chance to compete in the selection.
Inside the meeting hall at the king’s palace, King Thalirion and a figure clad in black, with a hood covering their head, were meeting.
"King Thalirion, I hope you are aware of what this means... I hope I don’t have to spell it out to you," the hooded figure said, sounding smug and arrogant.
This caused King Thalirion to clench his fist.
"Does this mean if we don’t want to become hunting dogs to the Hand, you and your kind will attack us... Is that what you are trying to tell me?" King Thalirion asked.
His aura started to rise, freezing the ground around his throne. The hooded figure remained unfazed despite the change in the hall.

"I am merely stating that should you or your people come across a human named Kent Madson, you can catch him or kill him... see him as a threat to your people because even if he caused no trouble here, he sure will bring one."
King Thalirion didn’t say anything. He just continued to look at the hooded figure with a cold gaze. The atmosphere remained tense, but at least he hadn’t attacked.
"In return, the Hand will give you a reward, and trust me, this reward, I am sure you will kill for it." The hooded figure paused, letting the King anticipate what this reward was about.
"How does a guaranteed spot in the Supreme Immortal Sect sound?" The moment the hooded figure said the words, the expression on King Thalirion’s face softened.

A guaranteed spot to send one of his own into the most prestigious sect in the world... If that is true, and in this case, he knew it was true, then wouldn’t that mean his chance to earn more resources from the Supreme Immortal Sect was guaranteed?
The King was immediately won over, and it was plain as day since the frozen ground melted and a sense of calm replaced the tense atmosphere.
"Are you sure..." the King asked.
"Dead serious... Even if you couldn’t kill or capture him, reporting it to us through this communication crystal will win you more than you could ask for.
But the spot to enter the number one in the world sect is only guaranteed if you manage to capture Kent Madson or kill him should you meet him before the others."
"So I wasn’t the only one given this offer," King Thalirion asked.

"Of course not, this offer was given to the Elves, Dragons, Demons, and some Beastskins. So, better take this seriously and don’t disappoint the Hand." After saying that, the hooded figure vanished from the hall, leaving a communication crystal.
The King took the crystal and stored it away.
"Just who is this Kent Madson who seems to have pissed off an organization like the Hand?" King Thalirion muttered.

The offer given to him was one he needed, regardless of how uncultured it sounded. If killing one person would get him a chance to get one of his own into the most powerful sect in the world, then he would do it.
"I don’t have to make a rash decision; I need to learn more about him before deciding. Someone who can make an organization like the Hand ask not one but multiple races to kill is not someone simple.
I better tread carefully, else I will doom my people." After saying that, he walked away. King Thalirion was not an idiot.

He knew who the Hand was and what they were capable of, so for such a terrifying organization to ask for his help — and the help of others — then the person they wanted dead or captured might be a fascinating figure worth learning about.
If only he knew the Kent he was just warned about was on his way to his kingdom.

Kent was only an hour out of the Elven Kingdom when he stopped. He wasn’t going to the Elven Kingdom, and since the Half-Elf Kingdom was located close to it, from the direction he would be appearing, he knew he would have to pass through the Elven Kingdom.
But he wanted to reach the Half-Elf Kingdom without having to go through the Elven Kingdom.

"Per this map, I can go through the Flame Valley, one of the most dangerous places in the world. Many come there to hunt flame beasts, and even the lucky ones get rare Flame Spirits after killing some Flame Beasts...
When one absorbs a Flame Spirit, it becomes their soul flame. Those who already have a soul flame can feed the Flame Spirits to their soul flame, making it grow stronger.
"I have a little over three days to get to the Half-Elf Kingdom... Passing through Flame Valley won’t be bad at all. I might even have fun on my way to shatter people’s dreams and aspirations."
A smile appeared on Kent’s face as he started moving in the direction of the Flame Valley. Now that he had arrived on the other side of the world, he must make the best out of it.

chapters.title: Chapter 700: Flame Valley [Bonus]
paragraphs: The Flame Valley wasn’t a place Kent was familiar with, so he merely followed the map to the location. However, upon reaching the place, he was greeted with a rather scorching sight.

Flame Valley was a vast and treacherous expanse of molten rock, volcanic fissures, and smoldering ash fields, situated between the jagged peaks of the Crimson Mountains and the ash-choked forests that bordered the Elven and Half-Elf kingdoms.

His enchanted eyes were only able to give him a little, but at least he knew the Half-Elf Kingdom was situated in the northern part of the Flame Valley, which could be reached without having to go through the Elf Kingdom.
He appeared in the southern part of the Flame Valley, meaning he must traverse the torturous expanse of vast, scorching land to reach his destination.
Of course, there was a red warning attached to the information he gathered.
⟦Danger: Entering the Inner and Core area of the Flame Valley is prohibited if you value your life⟧
Kent held a grin on his face as he read the message.
"Do I value my life?" he asked himself, and then, using Chaos’ voice, he answered himself.
"Probably not... But I better not die."

"Since this sounded harrowing, I might as well use this time to strengthen my Chaos Soul Flame. This way, I wouldn’t pale in comparison to those snotty kids who think they can measure up to my greatness."

After ensuring his life was precious and shouldn’t be taken for granted, he decided to brave the danger. Three days—that was a long time to go around the Flame Valley through the west if he wanted to reach the Half-Elf Kingdom.
But now, he wanted to go through the thick and thin, which was bound to be dangerous by all standards.

Just like that, Kent entered the scorching landscape fraught with jagged stones and spiked earth. The patches of what remained of the forest looked even eerier, considering the trees stood with their leaves burning.
The domain of flames had transformed everything, including the very process of growth. Naturally, this means bad news for Kent since everything is almost guaranteed to kill him.
However, there was a silver lining to it.
Despite its dangers, the moment Kent found himself in there, his Eternal Draconic Jade Body started to adapt to the flame.
⟦Intense Flame Energy discovered. Your Eternal Draconic Jade Body has started Adapting⟧
⟦Your Flame Resistance grows Stronger⟧
This means the deeper he went, the higher his chances of climbing the charts of flame resistance. Of course, in flame elemental cultivation, there is Flame Comprehension and Flame Resistance.
Comprehension is the act of learning how to use the flame element as a whole, while Resistance is how to resist and defend...
Having a high comprehension of the flame allows for more flexible handling of the flame element in attacks, while resistance provides a more robust defense against it.
Comprehension: Weak ↠ Medium ↠ High ↠ Super ↠ Perfect ↠ Transcendent ↠ Harmony ↠ Perfect Harmony
Resistance: Weak ↠ High ↠ Super ↠ Perfect ↠ Immunity ↠ Perfect Immunity
So far, Kent had started walking the Resistance path, but that was all he could do, as his comprehension would come about when he acquired a flame art and started mastering it.
As Kent moved deeper into the valley, the heat became unbearable, but after a few minutes, his body would adapt, and he would continue to move forward.
After moving about four miles deeper into the domain of fire, he encountered his first flame beast.
⟦Name: BlazeFang Wolf⟧
⟦Bloodline: None⟧
⟦Realm: Root Ascension (Lvl 4)⟧
⟦Flame Spirit: None⟧
It wasn’t that impressive, considering it had no bloodline and also wasn’t a flame spirit he could feed to his Chaos Flame. The beast was also just too weak for someone like Kent.
However, when it moved, Kent was taken aback by how fast it reached him. It was an instantaneous dash that brought it close to Kent, claws moving for a swipe.
Kent was quick, though, so he dodged effortlessly, causing the attack to land on the ground, creating a scorching shockwave.

Before Kent could move in for an attack, the ground where he landed burst open, sending him flying up. He was caught off guard, but thankfully, he was able to stabilize early to handle the third attack from the wolf.
"Damn, this beast is more ferocious than even the spiders me and the girls killed in the dungeon," Kent found it fascinating how the BlazeFang Wolf was fighting.
It first attacked with a claw mimicking the attack of a FlameClaw Wolf, then it followed with a tail attack, taking the classic move of Lava Serpents, who love to attack using their tails.

Those attacks mostly involve exploding the ground or throwing fire at their opponents. Then, when those two attacks were executed flawlessly, Kent found himself a few inches away from two piercing fangs of the wolf.
Many have fallen to this attack since, if care is not taken, the first two attacks would overwhelm you, and then your head becomes dinner for the cunning wolf.
However, Kent was no easy target, so he merely grabbed one of the fangs and yanked it out. Then, with a precise attack, he drove the fang through the neck of the wolf, ending it.
"That was dangerous to some extent," Kent couldn’t deny. He had nearly fallen victim to a cunning attack from a level 4 Root Ascension stage wolf, and that was just too shocking.
"Tower, how do you explain the battle just now?"
⟦The master had just experienced what it felt like to fight a beast located in one of the most hostile environments.
Depending on the environment you find yourself in, you learn to adapt... the BlazeFang Wolf adapted and even learned to wield the skills of different beasts.
It wanted to survive, so it learned, adapted, and hunted until it met you. However, that doesn’t mean it would have fallen if it had met someone weaker.
Just as you and your legion are growing beyond your limits, many others are also growing, adapting, and seeking greater strength.
So heed my warning and take a detour; trust me, it’s for your own good. But if you want to keep going deeper, then be ready to take every battle seriously, else you will learn it the hard way⟧
"No need to worry about me, though... but thank you for warning me. I will handle things according to how they appear."
Deep within, Kent was pumped for danger. He wanted his life to be in danger... he wanted to push his strength to the limit, and he wanted to know what it feels like to fight a life-and-death battle.

sentences.text: The Flame Valley wasn’t a place Kent was familiar with, so he merely followed the map to the location.
However, upon reaching the place, he was greeted with a rather scorching sight.

Flame Valley was a vast and treacherous expanse of molten rock, volcanic fissures, and smoldering ash fields, situated between the jagged peaks of the Crimson Mountains and the ash-choked forests that bordered the Elven and Half-Elf kingdoms.

His enchanted eyes were only able to give him a little, but at least he knew the Half-Elf Kingdom was situated in the northern part of the Flame Valley, which could be reached without having to go through the Elf Kingdom.
He appeared in the southern part of the Flame Valley, meaning he must traverse the torturous expanse of vast, scorching land to reach his destination.
Of course, there was a red warning attached to the information he gathered.
⟦Danger: Entering the Inner and Core area of the Flame Valley is prohibited if you value your life⟧
Kent held a grin on his face as he read the message.
"Do I value my life?" he asked himself, and then, using Chaos’ voice, he answered himself.
"Probably not...
But I better not die."
"Since this sounded harrowing, I might as well use this time to strengthen my Chaos Soul Flame.
This way, I wouldn’t pale in comparison to those snotty kids who think they can measure up to my greatness."
After ensuring his life was precious and shouldn’t be taken for granted, he decided to brave the danger.
Three days—that was a long time to go around the Flame Valley through the west if he wanted to reach the Half-Elf Kingdom.
But now, he wanted to go through the thick and thin, which was bound to be dangerous by all standards.
Just like that, Kent entered the scorching landscape fraught with jagged stones and spiked earth.
The patches of what remained of the forest looked even eerier, considering the trees stood with their leaves burning.
The domain of flames had transformed everything, including the very process of growth.
Naturally, this means bad news for Kent since everything is almost guaranteed to kill him.
However, there was a silver lining to it.
Despite its dangers, the moment Kent found himself in there, his Eternal Draconic Jade Body started to adapt to the flame.
⟦Intense Flame Energy discovered.
Your Eternal Draconic Jade Body has started Adapting⟧
⟦Your Flame Resistance grows Stronger⟧
This means the deeper he went, the higher his chances of climbing the charts of flame resistance.
Of course, in flame elemental cultivation, there is Flame Comprehension and Flame Resistance.
Comprehension is the act of learning how to use the flame element as a whole, while Resistance is how to resist and defend...
Having a high comprehension of the flame allows for more flexible handling of the flame element in attacks, while resistance provides a more robust defense against it.
Comprehension: Weak ↠ Medium ↠ High ↠ Super ↠ Perfect ↠ Transcendent ↠ Harmony ↠ Perfect Harmony
Resistance: Weak ↠ High ↠ Super ↠ Perfect ↠ Immunity ↠ Perfect Immunity
So far, Kent had started walking the Resistance path, but that was all he could do, as his comprehension would come about when he acquired a flame art and started mastering it.
As Kent moved deeper into the valley, the heat became unbearable, but after a few minutes, his body would adapt, and he would continue to move forward.
After moving about four miles deeper into the domain of fire, he encountered his first flame beast.
